item.title: No trip to Azerbaijan! Lamine Yamal, out of the Champions League 🤕
item.description: No trip to Azerbaijan! Lamine Yamal, out of the Champions League 🤕 FC Barcelona have released a new medical update that directly affects their starting lineup. Lamine Yamal will not be part of the Barça squad traveling to Azerbaijan for this Wednesday’s UEFA Champions League clash against Sabah . According to the club’s statement, the young forward has been experiencing mild discomfort in his right ankle. Although the issue is not serious, the medical and coaching staff have decided to act early and leave him at home purely as a precaution. The aim is to avoid any unnecessary risk on a long and demanding trip. With such a packed schedule, protecting the fitness of one of the team’s biggest stars has become an absolute priority for Barça. The positive news comes with an eye on the weekend. The club have confirmed that sitting out the European fixture will allow him to recover fully in just a few days, ruling out any more serious injury. Lamine Yamal will therefore be fully available to return to the squad this Sunday. The winger will rejoin the team to face Deportivo de A Coruña in domestic competition. This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. You can read the original version in 🇪🇸 here.

item.title: Barcelona confirm Lamine Yamal out of Champions League tie with Sabah and share injury update
item.description: BARCELONA, SPAIN - NOVEMBER 22: Lamine Yamal of FC Barcelona looks on during the Spanish league, LaLiga EA Sports, football match played between FC Barcelona and Villarreal CF at Spotify Camp Nou stadium on November 22, 2026 in Barcelona, Spain. (Photo By Javier Borrego/Europa Press via Getty Images) | Europa Press via Getty Images Barcelona have confirmed that Lamine Yamal will miss the club’s trip to Azerbaijan to take on Sabah in the Champions League. The club have issued a statement to confirm Yamal has a minor ankle injury and will sit out the game as a precautionary move. Here’s the club’s official statement: “First-team player Lamine Yamal is experiencing mild discomfort in his right ankle. As a precaution, he will miss the match against Sabah and will be available for next Sunday’s match against Deportivo.” MEDICAL STATEMENT First-team player Lamine Yamal is experiencing mild discomfort in his right ankle. As a precaution, he will miss the match against Sabah and is expected to be available for next Sunday's match against Deportivo. pic.twitter.com/FxBWxL2y98 — FC Barcelona (@FCBarcelona) November 23, 2026 Yamal was spotted having treatment on an ankle issue in the warm-up ahead of kick-off between Barcelona and Villarreal on Sunday. The teenager did go on to play the full 90 minutes as Barcelona came from 2-0 down to win 3-2 and take home all three points. Yamal will now be given a breather before hopefully returning to action at the weekend when Hansi Flick’s side face Deportivo in La Liga.

item.title: Lewis Hamilton says he could win record eighth F1 championship as Ferrari’s number one driver
item.description: Lewis Hamilton has suggested that a record-breaking eighth world title would have been within reach this season had Ferrari chosen to prioritise him over team-mate Charles Leclerc. His comments came after he collided with Leclerc for the second time in three races at the Las Vegas Grand Prix, an incident described as "completely unacceptable" by Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur . Stewards later penalised Leclerc for his role in the collision. Following his first victory for Ferrari at the seventh round of 23 in Barcelona , Hamilton moved 40 points ahead of Leclerc and sat 41 points adrift of Antonelli. Although the 41-year-old rejected claims he asked Ferrari to make him their lead driver, he suggested that, with the right backing from his team, he could have given Antonelli a proper run for his money. “I’ve never asked to be the number one,” said Hamilton. “I genuinely haven’t. But there was a point in the season where I was 40 points ahead (of Leclerc) and at that point, the fight was with me and Kimi. “I was the closest one to him. I was second for a long time in the year, and at that point I needed the backing to make sure we beat Kimi. “There were a few instances in the season – where, with the support – I think we could have beaten Kimi in that battle. “It’s not what I’ve asked for. But we shouldn’t have been able to come together (in Las Vegas). It should just never happen. I’ve said everything I can on it. And the question now should be for Ferrari.” Charles Leclerc collided with Lewis Hamilton at the Las Vegas Grand Prix Hamilton’s chances of finishing runner-up in the standings – his highest championship position since missing out on his eighth title to Max Verstappen in 2021 – now look shot following the Dutch driver’s brilliant recent form. Hamilton is 37 points behind Verstappen with only 50 points left across the remaining rounds, in Qatar and Abu Dhabi. Hamilton is three points clear of both George Russell and Lando Norris, with Leclerc 17 points adrift. Russell finished only ninth in Sin City after he pranged the barriers with just two laps remaining when a late move on team-mate Antonelli for second backfired. Max Verstappen delivered a masterclass to win in Las Vegas “I wanted that win,” said Russell. “It was a bizarre race, and I went for a high-risk move and paid the price. “Of course I’m disappointed with the outcome, however, I have no regrets. I fought and knew if I wanted the win, I needed to be in the top two positions into the final laps.”

item.title: Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain has been hard done by, he deserves to start
item.description: Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain has been hard done by, he deserves to start The OX proving that he’s been hard done by. He needs to be starting more games from here on in… Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain with his MOTM award on Saturday.Image Dafabet Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain is a class act, as the one time England international proved once again in the 4-1 victory over St Mirren on Saturday. The former Liverpool and Arsenal man opened the scoring in an overall terrific display which seen him awarded the Man of the Match award for the third time this season. Luke McCowan of Celtic congratulated by his teammates Celtic v St Mirren, Scottish Premiership, Celtic Park, 21 November 2026. Photo Mark Runnacles Shutterstock IMAGO Despite having built up his fitness significantly after his half season spell in Glasgow, followed by a full pre-season for the first time in a couple of years, the 33 year old has failed to string together a consistent run of games so far this campaign, being used mainly from the bench at the latter stages of games. But on Saturday he proved he still possesses that ability to pick a pass, and find the net as he rolled back the years with whilst not an outstanding display, it was a decent one all the same, and more than worthy of his player of the match award. Mika Baur of Celtic passes the ball during the UEFA Europa League match between Celtic FC and Besiktas JK at Celtic Park on November 05, 2026. (Photo by Zak Mauger/Getty Images) injuries to Mika Baur , and Benjamin Nygren has opened the door to the OX, and he will now surely be given the chance to put a run of games together in the coming eight weeks or so. Along with Callum McGregor , the Ox is not only a talented player but one who boasts a ton of experience, and has seen and done it all, something that will only benefit us as the games come thick and fast, both at home and in Europe. Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain. Dundee Utd v Celtic, Premier Sports Cup, Saturday 15 August. Tannadice. Photo by Vagelis Georgariou It’s just a shame that it’s taken a few injuries for him to get that chance, but that’s the perks of having a big squad, and Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain is a terrific option to be able to call upon in a time of crisis. I fully believe that he will prove his worth, and roll back the years in the next few months. He more than deserves the chance to show his undoubted class on a regular basis. item.title: How 49ers' Brock Purdy dissected Vikings' vaunted defense: ‘Best player in the game'
item.description: San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy throws a pass Sunday against the Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City. (Fernando Llano/Associated Press) MEXICO CITY – On Sunday night, a year after Brock Purdy joined teammate George Kittle for a youth clinic in Cabo San Lucas, Mexico, the San Francisco 49ers quarterback returned to the country to take a very menacing group of grown men to school. The NFL's "Mexico City Game" quickly became the Brock Purdy Game in a game against an opponent that was supposed to slow his league-MVP roll. The Vikings arrived with the NFL's top-scoring defense, a blitz-crazed unit led by mad scientist coordinator Brian Flores and Purdy drove Minnesota mad and crazy in a 35-10 romp at Estadio Banorte. The late-game chants from the raucous, pro-49ers crowd of 85,612: "MVP, MVP, MVP!" "Seemed like he played a lot better than a lot of other guys have versus them," head coach Kyle Shanahan said. That is correct, Kyle. Minnesota arrived allowing 14 points a game. Purdy capped two of the first three drives with touchdown passes of 17 and 8 yards to Kittle and the 49ers had 14 points in 15-plus minutes. The Vikings had allowed three passing touchdowns in their previous 27 quarters. Purdy had three scoring tosses with 2:14 left before halftime. "Best player in the game right now," wide receiver Mike Evans said. It's safe to say this: Purdy is the best quarterback Minnesota has seen this season. Purdy completed 21 of 26 passes for 255 yards and three touchdowns, posting a 146.0 QB rating. The Vikings had allowed an NFL-low 69.5 rating entering Sunday that Purdy more than doubled. The highest rating against them in the first nine games: Detroit's Jared Goff (88.1). "I thought every time I looked up, he was peppering completions," Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell said. "Total poise. Command." The Vikings' blitz-heavy scheme specializes in making QBs harried. On Sunday, however, Purdy completed 17 of 19 passes for 208 yards with two touchdowns when Minnesota sent five or more rushers, which it did on 20 of his 26 dropbacks, according to ESPN. Purdy's completion percentage (89.5) against pressure was the highest the Vikings had allowed since 2016. "Oh my gosh," Kittle said, "he was so good." A sampling of some of Purdy's greatest hits? In the second quarter, with a defender at his feet, Purdy, 6-foot-1, had 6-3 defensive lineman Jalen Redmond coming straight at him with arms raised. The solution: Purdy threw a 7-yard jump-pass completion to fullback Kyle Juszczyk . "We never recommend the jump pass," Shanahan said. "But when he pulls it off and it works, then we congratulate him." During a 98-yard touchdown march that bridged the third and fourth quarters, Purdy kept the drive alive with a thing of beauty on 3rd-and-9 from Minnesota's 42. With Redmond about to level him, Purdy fit a seed between cornerback Byron Murphy and safety Joshua Metellus for a 13-yard completion to wide receiver Keenan Allen. item.title: Real Madrid yet to make final decision about Nico Paz -report
item.description: Real Madrid are still monitoring Nico Paz’s performances with Como but have not made a final decision about whether or not the club will trigger their €80 million option to buy him back next summer, according to a report published today on AS. At Valdebebas, views regarding the Tenerife native remain unchanged. Indeed, doubts concerning a potential return have not dissipated. Club officials are acutely aware that the player seeks playing time and a prominent role, and at present, his prospective arrival would entail competing primarily with players such as Jude Bellingham or Arda Güler, with Brahim Díaz and Rodrygo also awaiting their opportunities. There is no indication whatsoever of a possible change of heart. Source: AS The same can be said about Franco Mastantuono and Jacobo Ramón, per that same report. It would be much cheaper for Madrid to bring them back but Los Blancos will keep monitoring the situation until next summer.

item.title: Lamine Yamal expected to miss Barcelona’s Champions League trip to Sabah
item.description: BARCELONA, SPAIN - NOVEMBER 22: Lamine Yamal of FC Barcelona looks on during the LaLiga EA Sports 2026/27 match between FC Barcelona and Villarreal CF at Spotify Camp Nou on November 22, 2026 in Barcelona, Spain. (Photo by Pedro Salado/Getty Images) | Getty Images Barcelona are expected to give Lamine Yamal a rest and not include the teenager on the trip to Azerbaijan to face Sabah in the Champions League this week. According to Diario Sport and Cadena Ser, the decision has been taken to given Yamal a breather and he will remain in Barcelona and not play in the midweek game. The report adds that Barcelona want to protect their star man at a hectic stage of the stage. The low temperature in Azerbaijan is also mentioned as a contributing factor in the decision. Yamal has had a few niggles in recent weeks. He missed Spain’s game over Czechia due to a knee problem during the international break but did return against England. The Barcelona star went on to feature against Villarreal on Sunday in La Liga but was spotted having treatment on an ankle issue during the warm-up at Camp Nou. Barcelona are due to fly out to Azerbaijan later today for their match on Wednesday in Baku.

item.title: VIDEO: Gary Neville slaps himself in the face TWICE during bizarre rant as Manchester United nightmare continues against Liverpool
item.description: Manchester United v Newcastle United - Carabao Cup Final - Getty Images Sport Gary Neville reached his breaking point on live television as he watched his former club Manchester United crumble during a humiliating 4-0 defeat to Liverpool at Anfield. The legendary full-back left fellow pundits stunned after resorting to physical outbursts to express his sheer disbelief at the defensive display. Red card and defensive collapse spark studio outburst Mauricio Pochettino's tenure at Manchester United suffered a miserable blow as Liverpool ran riot at Anfield. The visitors' plans unravelled inside 10 minutes when Leny Yoro was sent off for hauling down Alexander Isak after Matthijs de Ligt lost his positioning. A starting backline featuring Yoro, De Ligt, and Lisandro Martinez struggled against relentless attacks. Even introducing Harry Maguire failed to halt the onslaught as Liverpool exposed a defence weakened by another summer of neglect. Watching from the Sky Sports studio, Neville reached boiling point during the post-match debrief. His bizarre rant left Jamie Carragher laughing and drew amusement from the broadcast panel. Watch the clip Dissecting the collapse on Sky Sports, the former United captain took aim at the defenders' poor body language. He claimed the backline never looks alert during matches. "I never see any of them on their toes, alert, looking like they’ve got something fixed in here (points to his head)," Neville said. "I never see any of them look like that. They look like that…" Bruh! Man United players have traumatised Gary Neville. He is literally slapping himself on Sky Sports 😂😂😂 pic.twitter.com/b1uiOLEf3t — Jaja (@JajaBreed) November 22, 2026 Neville stared blankly for several seconds. He then slapped his own face twice while saying "wake up" each time, before finishing: "You play for Man Utd!" Defensive crisis leaves Pochettino in relegation trouble The loss leaves United in the relegation zone with just one win from 11 Premier League matches. They have also conceded more goals than any side across Europe's top five leagues. Neville was especially critical of Pochettino's decision to start De Ligt following a year-long injury layoff. However, the pundit acknowledged how tough it is to return after a year on the sidelines. "I have a lot of sympathy for him," Neville added. "It’s like playing football after having six pints. It’s a strange feeling. I have a lot of sympathy for him, it’s alarming to watch." Urgent defensive rebuild awaits Pochettino Pochettino faces an immediate battle to lift United out of the drop zone and build on a solitary league win from 11 outings. Fixing the leakiest defence in Europe's top five divisions will be his top priority. Carefully managing De Ligt's fitness after a year out will be crucial. Without rapid improvements at the back, United risk sinking deeper into a relegation fight.

item.title: The numbers behind Pulisic’s influence on Milan’s scintillating attack
item.description: The numbers behind Pulisic’s influence on Milan’s scintillating attack Christian Pulisic has contributed to a goal every 87 minutes for Milan this season, while the Rossoneri have scored 28 goals in 12 league games, nearly a club record. Milan secured a comfortable 5-1 win over Frosinone on Sunday, with Pulisic scoring in the second half. ITALY – OCTOBER 31: Christian Pulisic of AC Milan celebrates scoring his team’s first goal during the Serie A match between AC Milan and FC Internazionale at Stadio Giuseppe Meazza on October 31, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) The American has already scored five Serie A goals this season and, according to Gazzetta, has contributed to a goal every 87 minutes through either a goal or an assist. He has also scored in each of his last three Serie A appearances. The only time he had a longer scoring streak for Milan was between September and October 2024, when he found the net in four consecutive matches. ITALY – NOVEMBER 8: Christian Pulisic of Milan looks on during a warm-up session prior to kick-off in the Serie A match between Genoa CFC and AC Milan at Stadio Luigi Ferraris on November 8, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Simone Arveda/Getty Images) Pulisic’s scintillating performances have contributed to Milan’s strong attacking displays, with eight different players scoring in Serie A so far. The Rossoneri have scored 28 goals in 12 games; only twice in history have they achieved more: 29 under Nereo Rocco and Lajos Czeizler, who coached Milan in the 1950s.

item.title: Bremen back in business: From relegation fears to European dreams
item.description: Bremen back in business: From relegation fears to European dreams Bayern stumbled and Dortmund pounced, yet Bremen’s buoyant display in the Nordderby was the major talking point from this Bundesliga weekend. Spearheaded by Niclas Füllkrug, Die Grün-Weißen now find themselves in sixth position. It is a welcome change from last season’s relegation fight: a challenge overcome under Daniel Thioune, who recently signed a deserved contract extension. Quite rightly, Füllkrug’s ten goals from the same number of matches occupy the headlines. However, it is worth noting that Marco Grüll has made a significant contribution in finding the net twice and assisting on six separate occasions. With the prolific German striker providing a much-needed focal point, Justin Njinmah’s pace now poses even more danger to opposing backlines. Hamburg found out the hard way, as the dynamic winger struck twice in Sunday’s four-goal rout. It never ceases to amaze how much of a difference one summer can make. Karl Hein made his place between the sticks permanent, racking up two domestic clean sheets since. Matters further up the pitch have aligned with Chuki and Eren Dinkçi, both anchored by fellow new face Ludovit Reis. Austrian centre-back and long-serving club captain Marco Friedl also remains a constant presence. Hoffenheim and Leipzig have even fallen short at the Weserstadion, one of few remaining fortresses during this campaign. Four wins and a single draw – the latter coming against newly promoted Paderborn – put the team second on home form alone. Sitting in the European places despite injury setbacks makes this feat even more impressive. Jens Stage will be out until the new year, while Felix Agu is recovering from a calf issue. Mitchell Weiser came back from a lengthy spell on the sidelines, only to immediately experience a thigh problem in late October. Kicking off the next round of fixtures on Friday offers another opportunity to build on this progress and extend what can now affectionately be called the ‘Bremen bounce’ as a struggling Borussia Mönchengladbach come to town. Locked in their own fight for survival, the visitors will be hoping to show the same resilience as their hosts did not that long ago. With a firing Füllkrug in their midst, few would bet against the men in green and white impressing once again in front of such energetic support.

item.title: Lost to Pakistan, now what? How Tilak Varma-led India A can reach Asia Cup Rising Stars semi-finals | Qualification scenarios
item.description: India A suffered a 48-run defeat against Pakistan A in their ACC Men's Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026 Group B clash at the West End Park International Cricket Stadium in Doha on Sunday. The defeat has put their semi-final hopes under pressure, but they are still very much in the race for a place in the last four. Tilak Varma-led India A have one more group match to play. They will take on the United Arab Emirates (UAE) on November 24, with a victory enough to secure their qualification. Pakistan A, on the other hand, have qualified for the semi-finals after winning both their matches (vs UAE and India). Only the top two teams from Group B will progress to the semi-finals, scheduled for November 26 and 27. Asia Cup Rising Stars: Where do India A stand in the points table? Pakistan A lead Group B with four points from two matches. India A and Nepal have two points each, while the UAE are at the bottom without a win and are out of the semi-final race. Nepal kept their hopes alive with a six-wicket victory over the UAE earlier on Sunday. Pakistan A's win over India A took them into the semifinal. Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026: Group B points table Pos. Team Played Won Lost Points NRR 1 Pakistan A (Q) 2 2 0 4 +1.090 2 India A 2 1 1 2 +2.580 3 Nepal 2 1 1 2 -2.461 4 UAE 2 0 2 0 -2.061 India A's positive net run rate of +2.580 gives them a major advantage over Nepal and could prove decisive if the teams finish with the same number of points. Asia Cup Rising Stars: How can India A qualify for the semi-finals? India A still have multiple ways to reach the last four. Their match against the UAE will be particularly important. Here are the possible outcomes: 1. India A beat UAE and Pakistan A beat Nepal This is the most straightforward route for India A. India A win against the UAE will take them to four points and guarantee a semi-final spot. The result of the Pakistan A-Nepal match will not affect their qualification. 2. India A beat UAE and Nepal beat Pakistan A If Nepal upset Pakistan A, India A, Pakistan A and Nepal will all finish with four points. In that case, net run rate will decide the final standings. India A will be in a strong position because of their 306-run victory over Nepal earlier in the tournament. Their superior net run rate makes them favourites to progress. 3. India A vs UAE match is washed out and Pakistan A beat Nepal A washout will earn India A one point, taking their total to three. They will still qualify if Pakistan A defeat Nepal. Nepal will remain on two points, while India A will finish with three and secure the second qualification spot. 4. UAE beat India A and Pakistan A beat Nepal A defeat against the UAE will make things complicated, but it will not automatically end India's campaign. Pakistan A will finish with six points, while India A, Nepal and the UAE will all have two points each. India A will have the advantage because of their much better net run rate. item.title: Pio Esposito devastated despite historic Inter hat-trick as Cristian Chivu's men throw away points in eight-goal Atalanta thriller
item.description: Atalanta BC v FC Internazionale - Serie A 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Inter striker Pio Esposito struggled to hide his disappointment despite etching his name into the Nerazzurri record books during a chaotic Sunday night in Bergamo. The young forward became the first Italian to net a hat-trick for the club since the legendary Christian Vieri, yet his heroics were overshadowed by a defensive collapse. Nerazzurri collapse in Bergamo thriller Inter’s visit to the New Balance Arena on Monday night turned into a bruising encounter that exposed the fragile nature of their current defensive setup. Despite holding the lead on multiple occasions, Cristian Chivu’s side allowed the hosts to claw back into the game, eventually settling for a point in a dramatic eight-goal stalemate . The result left a bitter taste in the mouth of the visitors, who had appeared to be in total control for large periods of the match. "It is difficult to explain a result like this," a dejected Esposito told Sky Sport Italia . "We never managed to kill the game off definitively, and therefore something did not go well. In the end, we conceded four goals. It is not just about the defense; we must refine all the details together and we will sit down to analyze the problems we faced." Esposito matches Vieri record While the team result was disappointing, Esposito’s individual performance etched his name into the Inter history books. By scoring three times, he became the first Italian player to record a hat-trick for the club since Bobo Vieri. It was a display of clinical finishing that demonstrated why he is considered one of the brightest prospects in the national team setup, showing a predatory instinct that rarely gave the Atalanta backline a moment of peace. Reflecting on the milestone, the striker remained grounded, stating: "It's a beautiful thing but today I am finding it hard to enjoy it because we let two points be pulled away from us and my first thought is that we didn't manage to take the three points home. I hope that the best Pio isn't now, but day by day, and above all I hope that the goals can lead to victories." The forward targets consistency Esposito’s rise continues to be one of the few silver linings for the club during a period of inconsistency. His tally for the season continues to grow, placing him among the top Italian scorers in the division alongside the likes of Alphadjo Cisse and Antonio Raimondo. However, the player himself insists that personal accolades mean little if the team cannot find a way to stabilize their defensive performances in high-pressure situations. "In the heat of the moment, I really struggle to give an explanation," Esposito added. "We manage to create many chances and support the action well, but then we must be capable of maintaining the result and not allowing these matches to be reopened. I hope the best version of myself can be seen day after day and that my goals help the team win." Shift focus to crucial Stuttgart clash Foll

item.title: Aiden McGeady somewhat unfair with his Yang ‘low bar’ remarks
item.description: Aiden McGeady somewhat unfair with his Yang ‘low bar’ remarks Former Celtic winger Aiden McGeady isn’t shy in holding back his opinions, and now he’s had a say on a current Celtic first team player who he reckons is “low bar” and no more than a squad player… 3rd May 2026; Easter Road, Edinburgh, Scotland: Scottish Premiership Football, Hibernian versus Celtic; Ex Celtic player Aiden McGeady. Photograph by Vagelis Georgariou McGeady who was recently part of the Ex-Celts Tennents Sixes winning side didn’t hold back as he had a pop at South Korean international Yang, saying they need to aim higher in the upcoming transfer window. Yang Hyun-jun of Celtic recives a yellow card during the Scottish Premiership match between Celtic and Kilmarnock at Celtic Park on November 08, 2026. (Photo by Ian MacNicol/Getty Images) The former Ireland international, as reported by Glasgow World , said: “Look, I think Yang is a good squad player. I think last season it was a low bar when you talk about wide players. “Yang was probably the standout wide player, but for Celtic to be where they should be and want to get to, you need someone of a better quality than Yang.” “But I think Yang does his job well. He chips in with goals, works hard.” McGeady added: “I do like Yang, but Celtic need to aim higher.” 5th September 2026; The Marbill Coaches Stadium, Paisley, Scottish Premiership, St Mirren versus Celtic; Yang Hyun jun of Celtic celebrates after he shoots and scores in the 68th minute to make it 2-1 to Celtic. Photo Vagelis Georgariou Fairs, fair from McGeady who knows what it takes to play on the wing for Celtic having made over 250 appearances for the Hoops and winning several honours, but he’s a bit harsh on Yang in my opinion. 12 months ago we’d all have shared Aiden McGeady’s opinion on the South Korean, but he’s improved so much in the last year that he fully deserves his place in the Celtic first team. So much so that it was evident we missed him in his recent absence. Hyunjun Yang of Celtic controls the ball during the Scottish Premiership 2026/27 match between Celtic and Dundee at Celtic Park on August 03, 2026. (Photo by Ian MacNicol/Getty Images) Yang has shown great mental ability to earn a regular place in the Celtic starting XI, when it would have been easier to put his head down and get a transfer elsewhere. For that alone he deserves great recognition, and respect, not disrespected by saying he’s not good enough when he quite clearly is. Celtic v Hibs, 22 January 1983. Paul McStay (8) rushes to congratulate Celtic goalscorer George McCluskey (10).Photo The Celtic Wiki There is also not a single position in the Celtic side that could not be improved by signing a better – and usually more expensive – player for that position. item.title: Bad COP, Worse COP: What’s Next After Climate Talks Fail?
item.description: The collapse of marathon climate talks in Turkey has renewed questions about reform of their consensus requirement, and galvanised calls for legal action and ambitious side agreements between like-minded countries. The “conference of the parties” talks, better known as COP31, ended without agreement and two days over schedule on Sunday, as countries deadlocked on fossil fuels, finance, science and carbon-removing technologies. It was an ignominious end for an unusual dual-presidency shared by Australia and Turkey, and negotiations chair Chris Bowen, who is Australia’s climate minister, said it was “very disappointing”. For many observers, the outcome was the inevitable result of a process that has regularly been hamstrung by its insistence on consensus. “Decision-making that requires every country to agree on every comma is not fit for a climate emergency,” said Nikki Reisch, director of the Center of International Environmental Law’s climate and energy programme. Bowen identified the same issue. “The fundamental root of the problem is that when COP was created, for reasons I understand, it was made consensus only,” he said. “That’s a very tough ask.” ‘Significant reform’ COP31 President and Turkey’s Minister of Environment, Urbanisation and Climate Change Murat Kurum (C) attends a plenary session of the United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) at the Antalya Expo Centre, in Antalya on November 22, 2026. Sunday’s collapse has renewed calls for a reform to that consensus-based process, in which any one country, or a small minority, can nix progress. “It has been clear for years that the COP process is in need of significant reform,” wrote former US vice president Al Gore on X. He urged a “reinvigorated multilateral process that reflects the latest science and represents the will of the majority of the world.” But as Bowen noted, “you also need consensus to change consensus” — in other words, all countries would have to agree those reforms. He described that as a “particular challenge,” although others might characterise it as simply impossible. The COP31 talks deadlocked over multiple issues, notably whether the so-called cover decision would mention phasing out planet-warming fossil fuels. Several countries refused a deal without that mention, while others including Saudi Arabia were vehemently opposed to its inclusion. There were other serious faultlines, including the timing of scientific work from the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change, and language on carbon capture, a technology championed by the fossil fuel industry but criticised by some as costly and ineffective. Crucially for developing countries, there was also no progress on finance — the money badly needed to help countries transition energy systems and adapt to the natural disasters climate change is already worsening. “The fundamental problem for globally agreed climate policy is more starkly obvious than ever: fossil fuel powers will not agree to have their resource

item.title: How Missouri State star Kaemyn Bekemeier has mastered the NIL era
item.description: SPRINGFIELD —The world of college athletics is seeing young people profit from their play. Name, Image, and Likeness has taken over. While some athletes are receiving a flat check, others are using their marketing prowess to build brands and businesses. Enter Kaemyn Bekemeier, Missouri State’s star guard. The fourth-year player has one of the sweetest jump shots on the team. She has also created quite a brand for herself. “You have to step out of your comfort zone,” Bekemeier said. “I try to keep it as authentic as I can. I’m not going to promote something that I don’t genuinely love.” Missouri State soccer: Bears advance in NCAA Tournament after historic SLU win Bekemeier was Conference USA’s Preseason Player of the Year. She’s led the Lady Bears to a strong start with key wins over Saint Louis and Wichita State. Missouri State will take on its most formidable foe in the non-conference schedule on Thanksgiving Day. The Bears will face ranked Minnesota at 5:30 p.m. in Cancun, Mexico. The Lady Bears will also face Washington State on Friday, Nov. 27. While Bekemeier is draining shots on the court, she’s also created quite the business off the floor. The Republic native is arguably the best local athlete donning a Missouri State jersey. Bekemeier is on billboards across Springfield and Republic. It’s all been a fun side quest for her. It all started freshman year when local gas station chain Rapid Robert’s reached out to Bekemeier. “They wanted me to make a video and they left it up me. I made a video and they loved it,” Bekemeier said. “We’ve been partners ever since. I do multiple videos with them a month. Once I posted a few videos, more and more brands started to reach out.” Drury basketball: How KeShaun Thomas broke the Panthers scoring record Bekemeier has almost 11,000 TikTok followers and 5,000 Instagram followers. This is where she posts the majority of her content. She’s worked with local restaurants, banks and car dealerships across the Ozarks. It’s a lot more complicated than just creating a video. Bekemeier has video calls and many discussions before signing any contract. While many athletes have agents that take care of this part, Bekemeier is a one-woman show. She does it all for her NIL deals. “I’m very Type-A,” she laughed. “It’s helping me for when I get out into the real world. I have a content calendar. I’m very on top of things and my mom’s my photographer.” Brands are pitching ideas to Bekemeier consistently. She has had to find ways to wade through these waters on her own. She has some non-negotiables, and it all comes down to authenticity. She enjoys it when companies leave her room to be creative. On the court, Bekemeier thrives in transition when she can read and react with the ball. In content, she wants to showcase her creative side. “I don’t like it when it is super scripted, and they want you to say X, Y, and Z,” Bekemeier said. “I’m a busy student-athlete, so giving me time to go film, sit down, edit it and send it of

item.title: Meet the Gazette's All-Area Girls Soccer team
item.description: CHILLICOTHE — This past fall, the area was blessed with another stellar girls soccer season. Individual milestones, historic victories and record-setting runs were all a part of the fun. One area team — Westfall — advanced to a district title game, while the others continued to set a solid foundation for their futures. Meet the Gazette's All-Area Girls Soccer team, a cast that helped their teams reach their potential. Player of the Year: Kyleigh Mercurio, Westfall, senior With the ball at her feet, Mercurio was the most dangerous player in our area. The senior capped off her career by tallying 34 goals and 16 assists, leading the Mustangs to their first-ever district title appearance. She ends her career with 90 scores, leaving a lasting legacy. F: Elliana Myers, Unioto, senior Unioto scored 51 goals this past season and Myers was responsible for 31 of those scores, or 59.6 percent of the offense. She was the SVC POY and a first-team all-district honoree. F: Abby Acord, Piketon, junior Acord was a threat any time she touched the ball. The junior scored 22 times and passed out eight assists, helping her Redstreaks finish with six wins. She’ll be even better next fall. MF: Gabriella Mathis, Zane Trace, sophomore Some players do little things that you won’t see in the box score, but have a significant impact on the game. Mathis is one of those players. She earned all-league and all-district honors. MF: Emmie Secrest, Waverly, junior Secrest was consistently a glimpse of success for the Tigers this fall. She scored a team-high 11 goals and passed out a team-high four assists, earning herself all-conference and first-team all-district honors. MF: Jaylin Forbes, Piketon, senior Pound for pound, there may not be a tougher player than Forbes on this list. She controlled the middle of the pitch for the Redstreaks all year long, and added five goals for good measure. MF: Addison Wallace, Westfall, freshman For the next three seasons, Wallace is going to be a thorn in her opponents’ sides. Just a freshman, she turned in 21 goals and eight assists. Those numbers helped Westfall finish 13-6. Defender of the Year: Emma Slatton, Chillicothe, senior As a whole, Chillicothe withstood growing pains this past fall. But Slatton was a bright spot on a team that continued to show progress. The senior helped the defense pitch four shutouts and earned first-team all-league and all-district honors. She’ll leave a sizable void in the back. D: Abbie Proctor, Unioto, junior Proctor helped the Shermans’ defense allow 1.61 goals per night and was the leader of a back line that propelled Unioto to an 11-7 finish. Her speed and skill set her apart on a stout unit. D: Chloe Beatty, Chillicothe, junior Beatty quietly pieced together an impressive junior campaign. She was a staple of the team's defensive game plan, earning second-team all-district recognition. She’ll be its leader next fall. item.title: Elly Evarts still has a few things she'd like to help Gibsonburg do
item.description: How many times can you reach for a little more? You wouldn’t have thought Elly Evarts could work any harder. She’d already been recognized as basketball player of the year in the Sandusky Bay Conference three times. Then, Gibsonburg lost to Woodmore in a sectional final after beating the Wildcats twice during the regular season. Of course, Evarts strives for a player of the year four-peat. What she wants most, however, is a state championship. It might not have felt very close to the goal, but Evarts was determined to find another gear. She looks forward to an adjustment guarding the ball on defense. And coach Bo Evarts has more depth than he’s ever had. There’s a trio of freshmen ready to make noise immediately and three juniors who are prepared for new varsity roles. High school basketball girls Who to watch on the court for girls basketball in the area this season Sophia Foos, Chloe Jividen and Callie Diebler are freshman. Diebler’s father, Jeremiah Diebler, scored 1,000 points for the Golden Bears, before graduating in 2000. Jividen is the most well-rounded of the three, while Foos will be the first post off the bench and Diebler is a shooter. Evarts has taken all of them under her wing, while also making a concerted effort to expand her leadership role overall. When you can control a game, you are a leader. It’s up to you to determine what kind. Evarts is working to set an example at practice, as well as off the court. “She’s been through it all and she knows how girls treated her,” Coach Evarts said. “She was fortunate. Now, you want to show that to the younger girls. Basketball-wise, you can always improve. Ball handling and getting to the basket.” Evarts played through some nagging injuries the last two seasons, never at full strength. She seemed a little reluctant at times to attack with the ball, avoiding the discomfort that might come with contact. She shot 130 free throws as a freshman. Woodmore motivated her to get stronger. “I’ll try to draw more fouls,” she said. Evarts and senior Emma Jividen will be joined by juniors Mackenzie Muntz, Katie Hall and Ava Dawson as starters. Macey Kohler returns following surgery after a knee injury in the first matchup with Woodmore last season. Brooklyn Smith is a sophomore. Many of the girls have played together and all are familiar with winning at the lower levels. “We can move the ball and run a little more in transition,” Evarts said. “We have a deep bench. We can sub in and do the same thing. We can play fast and under control. Focus on defense and defense turns to offense. I hope that continues.” Evarts has 1,587 points, including 258 3-pointers in her career. She knows the mechanics. She works with trainer Ryan Christie to practice shooting off the dribble, with contact and off balance. “I know the form,” she said. “I’m trying to add some snippets to my bag.” She typically played off the ball on defense. She plans to pick up the point guard quickly, in order to slow opponents down. She has

item.title: Solape Fayemi Launches Saina Properties Across Four Markets
item.description: For many people, buying property is one of the biggest financial decisions they will ever make. Yet, knowing who to trust, how to verify ownership and whether a property is worth the investment can make the process overwhelming. It is a challenge Solape Fayemi hopes to address with the launch of Saina Properties , a real estate company now operating across Nigeria, the United Kingdom, the United States and the United Arab Emirates. Officially unveiled at an event held on 17 November at the Marriott Hotel, Ikeja GRA, Lagos, Saina Properties is built around a simple idea: property ownership should be guided by sound advice, proper verification and professional support, not just the excitement of closing a deal. For Solape, whose experience in the investment industry shaped her understanding of money, risk and wealth creation, the decision to establish the company came from recognising the need for a more considered approach to real estate. “We are not building Saina Properties because the world needs another company selling properties. We are building Saina because we believe there is room for a different kind of real estate experience. One where advice comes before the transaction, where due diligence is not treated as an inconvenience, and where people are encouraged to ask questions, understand their options and make informed decisions,” she said at the launch. That philosophy is reflected in the company’s three core areas of expertise: Advisory & Verification, Sales & Brokerage, and Developments . Rather than focusing solely on connecting buyers to properties, Saina brings together the guidance investors need to assess opportunities, the support required to navigate property transactions, and involvement in real estate development. The company is also building on experience gained before its official launch, having supported more than 25 clients with property opportunities across different markets. An important part of its proposition is the role of professional expertise in protecting property investors. Fayemi’s position raises a familiar question: people consult doctors for medical concerns and lawyers for legal matters, so why do some investors leave significant property decisions in the hands of relatives simply because they are available or familiar with the location? While trust and family relationships matter, they do not automatically translate into the technical knowledge needed to assess a property, verify its documentation or understand its investment potential. These decisions require proper checks, market understanding and accountability. With its operations spanning four markets, Saina Properties aims to support individuals and investors looking to navigate property ownership with greater clarity, whether they are buying, selling or exploring development opportunities. item.title: Former Real Madrid youth forward offers advice to JJ Gabriel ahead of high-profile move: ‘Signing for Los Blancos guarantees nothing’
item.description: Former Real Madrid youth forward offers advice to JJ Gabriel ahead of high-profile move: ‘Signing for Los Blancos guarantees nothing’ Former Real Madrid youth team forward Mink Peeters has reflected on the pressures of joining one of football’s biggest clubs at a young age, while offering advice to 16-year-old JJ Gabriel amid reports linking the Manchester United academy talent with a move to the Spanish giants. Peeters joined Real Madrid from Ajax as a teenager in 2014 and became part of the club’s youth setup. He helped the team win the 2017 Copa de Campeones and reach the semi-finals of the UEFA Youth League. However, his playing career was eventually cut short by persistent injuries and seven surgeries, with the Dutchman retiring in May 2026 at the age of 27. Peeters explains the reality of joining Real Madrid Speaking to AS , Peeters described his time in Madrid as an extraordinary experience but stressed that joining a prestigious club does not guarantee a successful professional career. Reflecting on what he learned during his time at the club, the former midfielder said, “It was one of the most incredible experiences of my life. But one of the lessons I share is that signing for a club like Real Madrid guarantees nothing. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Mink Peeters (@minkpeeters) “At that age, everything seems wonderful. But you’re not always aware of how much pressure, expectation, and uncertainty professional football brings.” Peeters also revealed that he has maintained contact with people at Real Madrid since leaving. He had even considered travelling to the Spanish capital for the upcoming Champions League meeting with PSV, although the plans ultimately fell through. “Yes, I’ve stayed in touch with people at Real Madrid over the years. In fact, I even considered travelling to Madrid for the match against PSV, and we were discussing how to make it happen. “Unfortunately, it didn’t work out in the end… But I still have a very good relationship with people at the club, and I hope to visit Madrid again soon.” Former Madrid youngster offers advice to JJ Gabriel With reports suggesting that JJ Gabriel could follow a similar path by joining Real Madrid at 16, Peeters urged the youngster to remain focused on his own development rather than outside expectations. “My best advice would be for him to follow his own dreams and stay true to himself. When you’re so young, and there’s so much attention surrounding you, everyone has an opinion. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Mink Peeters (@minkpeeters) “People will tell you what to do, where to play and what sort of player you should be. But, at the end of the day, it’s your journey. There’ll always be pressure and expectations, especially at a club like Real Madrid. “I hope he stays focused on his own development rather than on living up to other people’s expectations. I wish him an incredible future.” Peeters faces divided loyalties ahead of Real Madrid vs PSV The upcomi

item.title: Hamilton: Being Ferrari number one would have made me title contender
item.description: Ferrari driver Lewis Hamilton races ahead of team mate Charles Leclerc during the Las Vegas Grand Prix. (is associated with: «Hamilton: Being Ferrari number one would have made me title contender») Bradley Collyer/PA Wire/dpa Lewis Hamilton believes he could have won a record eighth Formula One world championship this season if Ferrari had prioritized him over team-mate Charles Leclerc. Hamilton’s claim arrived after he tangled with Leclerc for the second time in three races at the Las Vegas Grand Prix – a flashpoint Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur described as “completely unacceptable.” Leclerc was sanctioned by the stewards for his role in the collision. Hamilton’s maiden win for Ferrari at the seventh round of 23 in Barcelona took him 41 points behind Antonelli, and 40 ahead of Leclerc. And although Hamilton rejected the notion that he ever called on Ferrari to make him their number one driver, the 41-year-old suggested that, with the right backing from his team, he could have afforded Antonelli a proper run for his money. “I’ve never asked to be the number one,” said Hamilton. “I genuinely haven’t. But there was a point in the season where I was 40 points ahead (of Leclerc) and at that point, the fight was with me and Kimi. “I was the closest one to him. I was second for a long time in the year, and at that point I needed the backing to make sure we beat Kimi. “There were a few instances in the season – where, with the support – I think we could have beaten Kimi in that battle. “It’s not what I’ve asked for. But we shouldn’t have been able to come together (in Las Vegas). It should just never happen. I’ve said everything I can on it. And the question now should be for Ferrari.” Hamilton’s chances of finishing runner-up in the standings – his highest championship position since missing out on his eighth title to Max Verstappen in 2021 – now look shot following the Dutch driver’s brilliant recent form. Hamilton is 37 points behind Verstappen with only 50 points left across the remaining rounds, in Qatar and Abu Dhabi. Hamilton is three points clear of both George Russell and Lando Norris, with Leclerc 17 points adrift. Russell finished only ninth in Sin City after he pranged the barriers with just two laps remaining when a late move on team-mate Antonelli for second backfired. “I wanted that win,” said Russell. “It was a bizarre race, and I went for a high-risk move and paid the price. “Of course I’m disappointed with the outcome, however, I have no regrets. I fought and knew if I wanted the win, I needed to be in the top two positions into the final laps.”

item.title: Bayern urged to be patient with Musiala as lawyer dismisses wage cut
item.description: Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany (R) speaks with Jamal Musiala during the German Bundesliga soccer match between Bayern Munich and 1. FC Cologne at Allianz Arena. (is associated with: «Bayern urged to be patient with Musiala as lawyer dismisses wage cut») Tom Weller/dpa Germany sporting director Rudi Völler believes Bayern Munich should wait to see how Jamal Musiala progresses before discussing his contract situation, as the club toned down their rhetoric and a top lawyer said a wage cut was all but impossible. Germany and Bayern playmaker Musiala has been affected by absence seizures, a form of epilepsy, this season and the Bundesliga champions have openly wondered whether he will ever be the same player again. Honorary president Uli Hoeness spoke of a dilemma for the club, while chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen raised the prospect of talks with Musiala's management and family. Bayern board member Karl-Heinz Rummenigge also questioned the 23-year-old's lucrative contract signed just last year. "One should wait a bit," Völler told broadcaster Sky Germany late on Sunday. "He is playing. It is not as if he cannot play right now. Bayern need him for the next few weeks." Musiala, one of Bayern's top earners until 2030, missed the start of the season due to his neurological condition and then picked up a hamstring injury. He returned off the bench in the 1-1 home draw with Cologne on Friday and almost bagged a winner. Bayern are massively stretched following long-term injuries to key forwards such as Harry Kane, meaning Musiala will be needed more than ever in the coming weeks as they try to catch up with new leaders Borussia Dortmund. "I hope, as we all do ..., that it will be the way it was before," Völler remarked. "I am optimistic about that. He showed it before, even though he had the illness. We need Jamal in the national team too. He has shown what an exceptional player he is." At a visit to a fan club in the Bavarian town on Kronach on Sunday, Dreesen was more conciliatory. "We are giving Jamal time, and we have to do that," he said, according to Münchner Merkur/tz newspaper group. "It is like in your own company when someone is no longer able to do everything. That is a new situation in football, one we have to learn to deal with," he added. Addressing a fan who had asked a question, Dreesen said: "Your message is: speak, but speak a bit more quietly. I think everyone has understood that." Bayern have been widely criticized across the game for talking publicly about a possible contract renegotiation or wage cut. Leading German sports lawyer Joachim Rain told RTL that Bayern would have little chance of doing so legally. "A unilateral adjustment of the salary is not an option. Termination would only be conceivable in the event of permanent inability to play. There are currently no indications of this. Musiala is not permanently unable to work," he said.

item.title: ‘Maybe I have to change it’ – Hansi Flick plans penalty talks with Lamine Yamal and Raphinha after Barcelona beat Villarreal
item.description: BARCELONA, SPAIN - NOVEMBER 22: Lamine Yamal of FC Barcelona reacts after missing a penalty kick during the LaLiga EA Sports 2026/27 match between FC Barcelona and Villarreal CF at Spotify Camp Nou on November 22, 2026 in Barcelona, Spain. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) | Getty Images Hansi Flick has admitted he will speak to Raphinha and Lamine Yamal about penalty-taking duties in the wake of Barcelona’s 3-2 win over Villarreal on Sunday. Yamal missed a penalty in the first half at Camp Nou – his third miss from the penalty spot this year – leading Flick to admit he may have to make a decision when it comes to spot kicks. The Barcelona boss admitted that the decision on who takes penalties is decided by the players on the pitch but he may now intervene. “They are decided on the pitch,” he told reporters. “Maybe I have to think to change it, I am not sure. “I will speak with [Raphinha and Yamal] to see how we manage it in the future. Both of them are able to score penalties, but we have to think how we want to manage that in the future.” Raphinha has an excellent penalty record for Barcelona but we’ll have to wait and see who gets the nod the next time the Catalans are awarded a spot-kick. Who do you think should take Barcelona’s penalties? Share your thoughts in the comments below!

item.title: America 250: High school football Mount Rushmore of Holland position-by-position
item.description: While we are still in America's 250th year, I am still in the historic mindset. I have read about 15 books on the American Revolution this year, and as you saw during the summer, we did some 250 and Mount Rushmore lists for schools. One of the best parts about sports is being able to debate lists of the greatest athletes of all time. I am thankful for that this week, especially with all the division our country is experiencing right now. So let's come together to have some fun division on sports. The Holland area has had great tradition in high school football over the years. I am going to put together my Mt. Rushmore of high school football, position-by-position. Remember, this is my opinion. If you disagree, feel free to let me know, but please do so in a civil manner. Civil debates about sports are some of the best part about sports. More: America 250: High school boys sports Mount Rushmore picks for each school: Vote for top 5 So here we go with the Holland area high school football Mt. Rushmore lists: QUARTERBACK Corey Willis, Holland The most electrifying high school football player I have ever seen. He could beat you running, throwing, returning - just about every way possible. He led Holland to its best season in school history with 11 wins and a district championship. He went on to star as a receiver at Central Michigan and play for a season on the Arizona Cardinals practice squad. Carson Gulker, Zeeland West The quietest star I have covered; there was nothing quiet about his game. He used his ability as a runner and a thrower to become Zeeland West's top quarterback. item.title: Salary dispute holding up Ollie Bearman’s new Haas F1 deal
item.description: Motorsport photo Ferrari protege Oliver Bearman remains the only driver on the Formula 1 grid without a contract for 2027. It is a situation that would have been hard to imagine just a few weeks ago, given that his retention at Haas had been taken for granted since last summer. The announcement of Rafael Camara as Bearman's 2027 team-mate, which came ahead of the Brazilian Grand Prix, was expected to be swiftly followed by that of his British team-mate. Instead, the silence has dragged on to the point of becoming a talking point, even prompting rumours of Bearman driving elsewhere next year. The paradox is that Bearman and Haas have strong reasons to reach an agreement. Bearman has ruled out racing elsewhere in 2027, while Haas has long been expected to retain him, yet the negotiations have dragged on far longer than initially anticipated. In recent weeks, there has been speculation about the reasons for the deadlock, some linked to the contractual relationship between Bearman and Ferrari and to the future prospects of the 21-year-old Briton. According to information obtained by Motorsport.com, however, the issue holding up the signing does not concern the driver’s long-term future, but rather the financial terms of the deal with Haas. Ferrari has already exercised the option allowing it to retain Bearman within its driver programme. Given that Maranello has invested financial resources in the young Briton ever since he joined the Driver Academy in 2021, allowing Bearman to leave on a free transfer would be a big waste of all those efforts. Rafael Camara will finish the 2026 season for Haas as he prepares for his full 2027 debut alongside Oliver Bearman. Rafael Camara will finish the 2026 season for Haas as he prepares for his full 2027 debut alongside Oliver Bearman. Bearman could be in a position to leave Ferrari at the end of 2027 if he has not received a call-up to join the works team, but this scenario does not represent an obstacle to renewing with Haas, and there is no need to finalise his relationship with Ferrari in the short term – especially given that Lewis Hamilton is in the twilight of his career. The Scuderia has not ruled out any of its longer-term options. The immediate negotiations therefore centre on two parties: Haas and Bearman’s entourage. The sticking point is the salary offered by the American team, a figure that the driver and his staff do not consider commensurate with their expectations. This has led to a prolonged deadlock, despite both sides being aware of the need to reach an agreement. On the eve of the Las Vegas Grand Prix, Bearman made no secret of his disappointment at a situation that has now been dragging on for months. “There’s nothing new to say. To be honest, I’m rather disappointed to find myself here, at the twentieth round of the season, without a signed contract for next year. It’s a strange situation, but we’re getting there.” The Briton admitted that the uncertainty is becoming difficult to cope with,

item.title: Nigeria not ready to host World Cup, says FIFA president
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde FIFA President Gianni Infantino has said Nigeria is not currently ready to host the FIFA World Cup, citing the need for investment in stadiums, hotels, airports and transportation infrastructure. Infantino made this known in an interview with Arise News, aired on Monday, while responding to a question on what it would take for a country like Nigeria to host the global football tournament. “The key for hosting a World Cup is the infrastructure: the stadiums, hotels, airports, and transportation. This is where the investment is really necessary. “A country like Nigeria has the resources, the passion, and the will as well,” he said. Asked directly whether Nigeria was ready to host the World Cup, Infantino replied, “Today, no, but tomorrow, why not?” Nigeria last hosted a FIFA tournament in 2009, when it staged the FIFA U-17 World Cup, with Switzerland defeating Nigeria’s Golden Eaglets 1-0 in the final in Abuja. On his 10-year tenure as FIFA president, Infantino said the organisation’s growth and the expansion of its competitions reflected the work done under his leadership. “I think the facts really speak quite loudly here. Speak for themselves. The organisation of the World Cups, both for men and women, increasing the number of teams, increasing the competitive balance of these competitions, and the revenue news. “Of course, we moved from a bit more than 5 billion before I arrived to 16 billion in this last cycle,” he said. He added that football and FIFA had continued to grow, saying such progress required hard work and strict compliance with established standards. “Football is growing. FIFA is growing. This is not possible if you don’t work hard, but also if you don’t work in compliance with the highest possible standard,” he said. Infantino was in Nigeria over the weekend, where on Friday, he inspected the remodelled Warri City Stadium alongside FIFA Secretary-General Mattias Grafström. During the visit, h e praised Nigeria’s football heritage and the country’s contribution to the global game , noting that some of the world’s finest players came from Nigeria, particularly Delta State. “This stadium is fantastic. It has everything you can dream of. I just would love to wear some shorts and kick the ball. So as soon as it’s completely finished, we’d come and play games with all these great Nigerian legends who come from this region. “Not just in Nigeria, but some of the best players in the world come from Nigeria, come from Delta State,” he said. At the 48th Ordinary General Assembly of the Confederation of African Football in Abuja, on Saturday, Infantino also commended President Bola Tinubu for investments in sports facilities, saying they demonstrated the country’s commitment to its young population. “He is doing, together with all of you, fantastic job here in Nigeria, showing that you are a country projected into the future,” he said. item.title: Nothing will stop 750km Coastal Highway – Umahi
item.description: By John Alechenu, Abuja The Minister of Works, Senator David Umahi, has reaffirmed President Bola Tinubu’s commitment to completing the 750-kilometre Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, declaring that nothing will stop the project. Umahi spoke during an inspection of bridges on Sections 1 and 2 of the highway. The disclosure was made in a statement by Francis Nwaze, Senior Special Assistant to the Minister, in Abuja on Monday. He quoted the minister as saying, “Nothing will happen to the 750-kilometre Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, which passes through the nine coastal states. The President has directed that the project must be completed as envisaged.” Umahi described the highway as a profitable national investment capable of generating revenue, attracting private investors and unlocking tourism and industrial opportunities. “We are using concrete, and so we are entitled to carbon credits claim. We are also using solar instead of conventional electricity; we are entitled to carbon credits,” he said. He added that the superhighway would accommodate tourism facilities, factories, CCTV surveillance and other commercial infrastructure, with private investors already showing interest in recovering costs through investment arrangements. The minister disclosed that President Tinubu is expected to commission Section 1 this month or early December. He also clarified that the reconstruction of the East-West Road is an additional commitment by the President and does not replace or affect the Coastal Highway. He described the ongoing 1,068-kilometre Sokoto-Badagry Road as another major infrastructure undertaking of the administration, stressing that Tinubu is pursuing multiple major projects simultaneously. Umahi commended the President for the scale of infrastructure development and economic reforms, citing declining inflation, improved foreign exchange access for businesses and the absence of ASUU strikes. He urged Nigerians, particularly South-East residents in Lagos, to support the President, noting that the administration has delivered significant infrastructure projects to the region. Meanwhile, Umahi has ordered a three-week nationwide emergency rehabilitation of major federal highways ahead of the festive season and the January 2027 elections. He directed Zonal Directors, Controllers, Resident Engineers and contractors to return to the field immediately to ensure critical roads are made motorable across all six geopolitical zones. “I feel so sad that a contractor will be on site doing permanent work, yet some sections of the roads remain impassable. This practice must stop,” he said. He warned that contractors must not allow motorists to suffer on failed sections while permanent construction continues, directing that damaged portions be excavated and rehabilitated using appropriate materials and asphalt where necessary. Umahi directed officials to document the exercise, engage contractors, report challenges promptly and restore roads to acceptable motorab

item.title: Democrats win largest US House majority since 1992
item.description: Democrats have won the largest majority in the US House of Representatives in more than three decades, after Chuck Hubbard defeated Republican representative Virginia Foxx in North Carolina, US media projected on Sunday. The party won full control of both the House and Senate in a sweeping midterm rout with a landslide of upsets that delivered a crushing rebuke of President Donald Trump and his Republican Party. CBS News and NBC News projected Hubbard’s win on Sunday, securing the Democrats a 258th seat in Congress’ 435-member House. The majority is the largest won by either party since 1992, when Bill Clinton won the presidency and Democrats won a total of 258 seats. “House Democrats have just secured the largest majority any party in Congress has held this century. BOOM,” House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries said in a post on X. Sunday’s result came after Foxx requested a recount. Hubbard said Sunday that he had spoken with Foxx, who “graciously conceded following the results of the recount process.” “Let me be the first to thank Congresswoman Foxx for her decades of service and countless sacrifices,” he added on X. The Democratic victory hands the party the power to block Trump’s agenda and investigate alleged corruption for the last two years of his presidency. The midterm results reflected deep anger over living costs, tariffs and Trump’s war against Iran, which has sent fuel prices soaring and compounded dissatisfaction with an already deeply unpopular president. item.title: Thousands Evacuated After ‘Unknown Substance’ Released At UK Concert
item.description: Thousands were evacuated from a concert at the UK’s largest indoor arena after an “unknown substance” was released and several people reported suffering side effects, police said Monday. Some 12,000 people were attending the Sunday night show by US rapper Don Toliver at the Co-op Live arena in Manchester, northwest England. Emergency services were called after “reports of people in the crowd suffering effects from an unknown substance”, said Manchester police, which declared a major incident at the scene. “Several people were treated on site, and one has been taken to hospital at this time,” Greater Manchester Police’s Steph Parker said, adding that the force was trying to “understand what this substance was”. Emergency workers respond to an incident during a concert by rapper Don Toliver at Co-op Live on November 22, 2026 in Manchester, England. Concert goers were evacuated from the US rapper’s Manchester concert after reports of gas being released into the crowd. Don Toliver is partway through the UK leg of his Octane World Tour. (Photo by Ryan Jenkinson / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP) The venue, which bills itself as the country’s largest live entertainment arena, said it was working with police to “identify the cause of the incident”. The regional ambulance service said it assessed more than 50 people at the scene, including some reporting “eye and respiratory symptoms”, with “decontamination” being carried out at the venue. Toliver, an American singer who has collaborated with musicians Travis Scott and Justin Bieber, is currently on the second leg of his “Nitrous” world tour and scheduled to play in London on Monday. item.title: How Mary Akinwola Graduated with a Distinction from Oxford After Receiving Multiple Scholarships
item.description: Mary Akinwola graduated from the University of Oxford after receiving the Chevening and Mastercard Foundation Scholarships. My name is Mary Akinwola. I’m a physiotherapist, a strategy consultant, a healthcare entrepreneur, and I recently graduated from the University of Oxford with a distinction in Health Service Improvement and Evaluation. I have probably said that last part a hundred times since getting my results, and honestly, I don’t think I’m tired of saying it yet. Haha! One thing about me is that I like to be involved. I am sometimes curious about things that have absolutely nothing to do with what I’m supposed to be doing, and I genuinely enjoy working with people. I like organising things, bringing people together, and seeing an idea move forward to get accomplished. So I have known that going to Oxford was never going to be just about getting a master’s degree. Let me explain how I ended up there. I studied Physiotherapy at the University of Ibadan, where I graduated with First-Class Honours. During my undergraduate years, I was involved in quite a lot outside academics: student leadership, journalism, research, community health programmes and advocacy. My involvement in community health exposed me to how differently people experience healthcare depending on where they live, what they can afford and what information they have access to. I loved being a physiotherapist, and that allowed me to interrogate questions that went beyond individual patient care. Why do some people receive good healthcare while others struggle to access even basic services? How do we make healthcare more affordable? What role can technology play? And why do some seemingly good healthcare programmes struggle to produce lasting change? Eventually, I realised I wanted to study and work in a field that constantly seeks to improve health systems. I researched different programmes across the US and UK, hoping to study at institutions that have international audiences where I could build a diverse perspective in health. I came across the MSc in Health Service Improvement and Evaluation at the University of Oxford’s Nuffield Department of Medicine. It aligned with many of my interests, so I applied. I also needed a scholarship because, quite frankly, I couldn’t afford Oxford. It was a humbling and affirming process. I was awarded scholarships such as the Chevening Scholarship and two Oxford-based scholarships. I still feel fortunate to have received and chosen the Mastercard Foundation-Africa Oxford Initiative Scholarship, which fully funded my studies. I am deeply grateful for that opportunity. Now, I think it’s important to say that I was very excited about the academic programme. I wanted to understand healthcare systems better, learn new research methods and become more effective at designing and evaluating healthcare services. However, I was also very excited about everything else. I was going to be at Oxford! There were going to be people from different countries

item.title: African players in Europe: Mixed fortunes for Nigerian Awoniyi
item.description: Nigerian Taiwo Awoniyi scored for Coventry City and later had to be substituted after collapsing in a Premier League victory over Crystal Palace at the weekend. AFP Sport highlights African headline-makers in the major European leagues: ENGLAND TAIWO AWONIYI (Coventry City) The striker scored his third goal for Coventry in a 3-2 win against bottom club Palace, but his afternoon came to a bizarre premature end. Awoniyi netted in the fifth minute with a close-range finish into the far corner from Jack Rudoni’s pass to put Coventry 1-0 up at the CBS Arena. But the 29-year-old, signed from Nottingham Forest in the close season, was forced to miss the last 45 minutes after going down clutching his leg in pain while the players were lining up to start the second half. Awoniyi had to be helped up off the ground by two Palace players and limped off, forcing bemused Coventry boss Frank Lampard to make an unexpected substitution. Lampard admitted afterwards that Awoniyi felt a slight problem with his ankle from the first half. SPAIN YASSIR ZABIRI (Racing Santander) Moroccan forward Zabiri struck twice in the opening stages to help Santander beat Real Sociedad 3-2 in La Liga. The 21-year-old, on loan from Rennes, climbed to 11 league goals and trails only Raphinha and Kylian Mbappe in the Spanish scoring charts. Zabiri smashed home in the sixth minute for the opener and two minutes later was alert to pinch the ball from Real Sociedad’s goalkeeper and roll it into the empty net for his second. GERMANY JUMA BAH (Augsburg) Sierra Leone and Augsburg centre-back Bah netted his first goal since arriving on a season-long loan from Manchester City in his side’s 3-1 home romp over Mainz in the Bundesliga. With Augsburg 1-0 up, Bah was on the spot to prod a loose ball across the line from a corner to give the hosts their second. FRANCE PATRICK ZABI (Paris FC) Ivorian Zabi opened the scoring just after half-time as second-placed Paris FC hammered lowly visitors Angers 4-0 to lie second in Ligue 1 after 11 rounds, three points behind European champions Paris Saint-Germain. A cross was nodded into the path of the 20-year-old, and he slammed the ball into the net. BOULAYE DIA (Lorient) Dia, a 2022 Africa Cup of Nations champion with Senegal, put Lorient ahead away to Rennes in a 1-1 draw between mid-table clubs. Tunisian Montassar Talbi equalised in the final minute of the first half. The post African players in Europe: Mixed fortunes for Nigerian Awoniyi appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027: Tinubu won’t be included in my national unity govt — Makinde
item.description: The presidential candidate of the Action Peoples Movement (APM), Seyi Makinde, has ruled out including President Bola Tinubu in his proposed government of national unity if elected in 2027, accusing the president of failing to honour an agreement they reached ahead of the 2023 election. Makinde, however, said he would consider appointing capable members of the All Progressives Congress (APC) into his government, insisting that there were decent people in the ruling party who could contribute to governance. He stated this during an interview on The Rooftop Podcast, where he was asked whether he would bring former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, Peter Obi and Tinubu into his government if elected. “Perhaps not President Tinubu, but there are still decent people in APC as well. I’ll tap them and they are Nigerians,” Makinde said. Asked whether he did not consider Tinubu decent, the governor said his position was informed by his experience working with the president during the 2023 election, when an agreement on a government of national unity was allegedly reached but not fulfilled. “Well, not in that context. I mean, I worked for him in 2023. We agreed on a government of national unity. He did not fulfil it,” he said. Makinde explained that the agreement was part of the position taken by the PDP G5 governors, who broke ranks with the party’s leadership ahead of the 2023 presidential election, saying they wanted an inclusive government that would draw competent Nigerians from across the country, irrespective of political affiliation. “We came from the PDP as G5 and we said, ‘Look, this is not going to be a government of APC. It should be a government where you tap people from all across the country. Go to every corner of the country, pick and choose people that can help you know to sort some of this out,’” he said. The APM candidate said the idea of a government of national unity was not new, citing the administration of the late military Head of State, General Sani Abacha, as an example of efforts to bring prominent Nigerians into government to ease political tensions. He recalled that following the annulment of the June 12, 1993 presidential election, Abacha appointed prominent figures, including former Lagos State governor Lateef Jakande and businessman Alex Ibru, to his government. Makinde said the appointments were intended to calm tensions and pacify aggrieved Nigerians. “And it’s been done before. After the annulment of the June 12, 1993 elections, and General Abacha came into government, they went and tapped Alhaji Jakande, Alex Ibru, all of those were geared towards bringing down the temperature in the country and ensuring that where there are angry people, they are being pacified,” he said. He accused Tinubu of failing to replicate such an inclusive approach, alleging that the president’s appointments were largely drawn from his political circle. “Tinubu didn’t do that at all.
