item.title: ‘Monies Borrowed Are Being Used For Investments, Infrastructure’, Umahi Inspects Coastal Road Bridges
item.description: The Minister for Works and Infrastructure, David Umahi, has defended the external borrowings of President Bola Tinubu, saying the monies are being invested in the building of infrastructure across the country. Umahi revealed this as he inspected the Coastal Road Bridges on Sunday. According to him, the road projects are not the only investments President Tinubu is spending the borrowed monies on, as the Federal Government also has the vision of investing in housing for rentals. Umahi while inspecting the coastal road bridges on Sunday, November 22, 2026. “As far back as six months, section one was already fully completed. Section two, which is about 53 kilometers, is also already completed. It has road architecture such as solar lights, underground drainage, and the walkway. “So, it’s something that is out of this world in terms of performance, where you have over 200 kilometres plus being done within two and a half years. It’s a performance that no other contractor in Africa has been able to achieve. “I have bragging rights as the Minister of Works over these projects because I am very proud of them. I have bragging rights for the President because when you are on this coastal way, it is quite relieving. “Imagine if we can go all the way from Lagos to Calabar on this kind of road. All these roads are investments of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. And when you ask about the monies which are being borrowed. They are being used for infrastructure. They are being used for investment in infrastructure. “And investors are asking how they can return the investments on this road. But we are still considering their request because we want to install CCTV, we want to rent houses. We want to buy land where we can have a lot of facilities for tourism, factories, and others. “And these projects are profit-driven for the Federal Republic of Nigeria. One of the completed coastal road bridges inspected on Sunday, November 22, 2026. This is as President Tinubu has asked the House of Representatives to authorise FG to access $7.71bn (N10.79 trillion) in external loans already captured in the 2026 Appropriation Act, with Eurobond issuance expected to be a major funding option. The request was contained in a letter to the Speaker of the House, Tajudeen Abbas, and was read during last Wednesday’s plenary. Tinubu said the proposed borrowing would help finance part of the Federal Government’s budget deficit and fund projects across critical sectors, including defence, transportation, agriculture, power, education and health. item.title: 2027: Why Nigerians should prefer me to Obi-Kwankwaso – Makinde
item.description: By Bayo Wahab Oyo State Governor and Allied Peoples Movement (APM) presidential candidate, Seyi Makinde, has explained why Nigerians should choose his ticket with former Kano State governor, Ibrahim Shekarau’s associate Daura, over the Peter Obi-Rabiu Kwankwaso ticket in the 2027 presidential election. Makinde cited the historic alliance between the Southwest and North, his experience in governance, youthful energy and plans for national unity as key advantages of his candidacy. Speaking on The Rooftop Podcast, the governor said the relationship between the two regions had helped Nigeria maintain stability during difficult periods, arguing that his ticket was positioned to sustain that tradition. “Apart from the traditional Southwest-North alliance, because that alliance has always provided stability for Nigeria in time of crisis in the past,” Makinde said. He recalled Nigeria’s first military coup, arguing that the Southwest and North had historically played significant roles in efforts to preserve the country’s stability. “If you even go back to the first military coup in Nigeria, the people that were wasted were basically the north and southwest, because we’re always in the forefront of stability for the country, and that is what we have brought to the table,” he said. Makinde also pointed to his performance in Oyo State and what he described as the youthful energy of his ticket, saying his administration’s achievements and commitments could be measured against documented promises. He said his political agenda was designed to allow Nigerians hold him accountable for his promises, rather than rely solely on campaign rhetoric. The APM candidate also outlined his proposed transitional government of national unity, saying it would address Nigeria’s political and security challenges through a broader national consensus. Makinde said he was willing to lead such a transition but would not remain in office to benefit from its eventual outcome, arguing that doing so could compromise his decisions. “I can lead it, but I will not be a beneficiary of the outcome because if I’m looking at myself benefiting from that outcome, it may cloud my judgment and also block how I will take that decision,” he said. He said the proposed arrangement was necessary because insecurity and other problems affecting Nigeria were not confined to any particular region. “And a government of national unity, because, you know, you look at insecurity and things fueling it all around the country. It’s not limited to any area,” Makinde said. The post 2027: Why Nigerians should prefer me to Obi-Kwankwaso – Makinde appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo Kano State Governor, Abba Kabir Yusuf, has accused his former political mentor, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, of reneging on an agreement to defect to the All Progressives Congress (APC) after the 2023 governorship election. Yusuf, who made the allegation in an interview with BBC Hausa, said Kwankwaso personally asked him to approach President Bola Tinubu and assure him that they would join the APC if the President did not interfere in the legal battle over the Kano governorship election. The governor said the agreement was reached after the 2023 election, when his victory over the APC candidate, Nasiru Yusuf Gawuna, was being challenged in court. According to Yusuf, Kwankwaso initiated the arrangement and asked him to swear by the Holy Qur’an that they would return to the APC if the judicial process was allowed to run its course without interference. “Kwankwaso himself sent me to Tinubu and asked me to tell him that we had made that promise. He even wanted me to swear by the Holy Qur’an that if God granted us victory, we would all come together,” Yusuf told the BBC. He said he honoured the agreement and subsequently assured Tinubu of their intention to defect. Yusuf added that Kwankwaso also held several meetings with the President and sent delegations to discuss the proposed political realignment. The governor, who formally defected from the New Nigeria Peoples Party (NNPP) to the APC on January 26, 2026, insisted that he did not betray his former political benefactor but fulfilled an agreement that Kwankwaso later abandoned. He also dismissed suggestions that his defection was a political arrangement aimed at weakening the opposition or distracting the public, maintaining that Kwankwaso was aware of the discussions and arrangements leading to the move. Yusuf, however, said some remarks allegedly made by Kwankwaso shortly after he had assured Tinubu of their planned defection undermined the arrangement. He said the comments were communicated to the President and reportedly did not go down well with him. On his relationship with Kwankwaso since their political separation, Yusuf said they had occasionally communicated, adding that he sometimes sent messages to greet his former mentor. He declined to discuss publicly allegations that Kwankwaso had exerted undue influence over his administration or prevented him from exercising his responsibilities as governor, saying such matters were better left outside the media. Marital crisis The governor also spoke about the reported marital crisis between him and his wife, Zainab Musa Kwankwaso, a niece of the former Kano governor. Yusuf said their marriage, which began about 20 years ago, produced children, but difficulties eventually emerged in their relationship. He alleged that his wife’s belongings were removed from his residence and that she was taken away without his knowledge. item.title: Abuja entrepreneurs struggle with soaring costs, shrinking demand
item.description: Abuja entrepreneurs struggle daily as rising costs, shrinking purchasing power and inconsistent income threaten the survival of enterprises they have spent years building. From bakers battling unreliable electricity and rising ingredient prices to fabric sellers struggling with customers who buy on credit and fashion designers waiting for payments, entrepreneurs across different sectors say the harsh economic climate is making it increasingly difficult to sustain their businesses. They say their income is often insufficient to cover the cost of running their businesses, leaving them with little profit and, in some cases, mounting debts. Aisha Dikko, a baker and food vendor, said her journey into business had been marked by sacrifices, unexpected challenges and lessons she never anticipated when she started. Inspired by her mother, who was also a baker, Dikko said what began as a passion gradually developed into a business. However, she admitted that she had initially underestimated the demands of running an enterprise. “I thought it would be relatively easy. People loved my cakes and small chops whenever I made them at home, so I assumed turning that into a business would be straightforward,” she said. She said she soon realised that running a business required much more than the ability to bake, as she had to learn about pricing, marketing, customer relations, production and financial management. Although she has recorded some growth over the years, Dikko said fluctuating prices of ingredients and supplies remained a major challenge, with the cost of restocking often changing from one purchase to another. Beyond rising costs, she said the declining purchasing power of customers had also affected her business, with some making unrealistic offers for products whose production costs were considerably higher. Dikko recalled an instance when a prospective customer offered N70,000 for desserts for 300 guests, even though her estimated cost of providing desserts for just 100 guests was about N300,000. She further explained that electricity had been one of her most difficult operational challenges. The situation, she added, became so frustrating that she considered abandoning the business. The installation of solar power by her husband, however, provided some relief and enabled her to continue operating from home, although she still relies on gas and an inverter for some operations. She called on the government to provide more practical support for small businesses, arguing that access to loans alone would not address the challenges entrepreneurs face. For fabric seller Aisha Kabir, the challenge of keeping a business afloat is largely tied to cash flow, particularly as more customers struggle to pay for goods purchased on credit. Kabir, who has been in the fabric business for over a decade, said sales on credit had made it increasingly difficult to maintain consistent cash flow. item.title: Senate committee hails Air Peace over ₦80,000 military fare
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Senate Committee on Army has commended Air Peace and its Chairman, Dr Allen Onyema, for introducing a discounted one-way domestic air fare of ₦80,000 for serving and retired personnel of the Nigerian Armed Forces. The committee also urged other airlines and corporate organisations in the country to emulate the gesture as part of efforts to improve the welfare of military personnel and veterans. The commendation was contained in a statement issued on Sunday by the Chairman of the committee, Senator Abdulaziz Musa Yar’Adua, representing Katsina Central Senatorial District. According to the statement, the initiative was unveiled on November 16, 2026, during the 2026 Chief of Defence Intelligence Annual Conference in Abuja. The committee said the discounted fare was available to eligible military personnel who had served in the Nigerian Armed Forces since 1960, across all domestic routes. It added that Air Peace would also bear the cost of tickets for regional and international flights, with beneficiaries required to pay only applicable taxes and charges. Describing the initiative as a patriotic gesture, the committee said it was a practical demonstration of appreciation for the sacrifices made by serving and retired military personnel in defending the country’s sovereignty and territorial integrity. It noted that members of the Armed Forces had continued to make enormous sacrifices, often at great personal cost, and deserved tangible support that would improve their welfare and that of their families. “By reducing the burden of air travel, Air Peace has demonstrated that patriotism is not only spoken in times of ceremony, but shown in practical action that touches the lives of those who serve,” the statement said. The committee particularly praised Onyema for what it described as his consistent commitment to humanitarian causes, national development and support for the Nigerian military. It also endorsed the airline chairman’s call for the military leadership to establish a robust verification system to ensure that only genuine beneficiaries access the concession. According to the committee, such a mechanism would help make the initiative sustainable, transparent and free from abuse. It appealed to other airlines and corporate organisations to support the Armed Forces, describing the welfare of serving personnel and veterans as a collective national responsibility. “The private sector has a critical role to play in complementing the efforts of the Federal Government in improving the welfare and morale of our troops and veterans,” it said. The Senate committee assured Air Peace of its support and readiness to work with the airline, the Ministry of Defence and the Service Chiefs to ensure the smooth implementation of the initiative. It reiterated its appreciation to the airline’s management for the gesture, describing it as a meaningful tribute to Nigeria’s military personnel. The post Senate committee hails Air Peace over ₦

item.title: FG partners world’s largest pivot irrigation maker
item.description: By Favour Ulebor The Federal Government has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Valmont Industries Inc., the world’s largest manufacturer of pivot irrigation systems, to accelerate the implementation of its flagship Irrigate Nigeria Programme. The agreement also provides for the establishment of an irrigation equipment production plant in Nigeria in partnership with the National Agency for Science and Engineering Infrastructure (NASENI), as part of efforts to boost local manufacturing and reduce dependence on imported irrigation technology. The Presidential Implementation Committee on Technology Transfer (PICTT) signed the agreement with Valmont at the weekend. In a statement issued by NASENI on Sunday, the Chairman of PICTT, Dr Dahiru Muhammed, who is also coordinating the implementation of the Irrigate Nigeria Programme, said the agreement formally brought Valmont, through its Valley Irrigation brand, on board as a major partner in developing irrigation infrastructure across the country. Muhammed, who signed the agreement alongside Valmont’s Regional Vice President for the Middle East and Africa, Mr Kalle Autto, described the partnership as a significant step towards expanding mechanised irrigation in Nigeria. He said: “This MoU officially brings the biggest pivot irrigation manufacturer in the world on board as a major partner in building irrigation infrastructure across Nigeria under the Irrigate Nigeria Programme, the flagship irrigation programme of this administration.” He explained that beyond developing irrigation infrastructure, Valmont had agreed to work with NASENI to establish a local production facility for irrigation equipment. “Just as importantly, this partnership comes with the transfer of know-how and capacity building for Nigerians, which is precisely what technology transfer is all about,” he added. The agreement also provides for a pilot irrigation programme covering 40,000 hectares in Adamawa State. The project will be implemented in collaboration with the Nigeria Incentive-Based Risk Sharing System for Agricultural Lending (NIRSAL) and the National Agricultural Development Fund (NADF). While PICTT will lead the overall implementation of the programme, NASENI will drive the adoption and domestication of the technology. The partnership is also expected to create opportunities for collaboration with the University of Nebraska and the Robert B. Daugherty Water for Food Global Institute on sustainable irrigation systems and water resource management. Muhammed said key stakeholders had already expressed interest in expanding irrigation infrastructure through the partnership, describing the development as a vote of confidence in the programme. Officials said the agreement would help improve agricultural productivity, strengthen national food security and promote the sustainable management of water resources in line with the Federal Government’s agricultural transformation agenda. item.title: Troops rescue 18 abducted children, hunt for four others in Kaduna
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi Troops of the Nigerian Army under Operation Fansan Yamma have rescued 18 children abducted by suspected terrorists in Kaduna State, while intensifying efforts to secure the release of four others still held by the fleeing kidnappers. The children, members of the Boys’ and Girls’ Brigade, were reportedly abducted early Sunday, November 22, 2026, while participating in a morning group road walk at Mother-Cat Community in the Kachia/Kajuru general area of the state. Confirming the rescue in a statement on Sunday night, the Acting Director, Army Public Relations, Colonel Appolonia Anele, said troops of the 1 Division Nigerian Army, operating under Sector 1 of Operation Fansan Yamma, launched a rescue operation shortly after receiving a distress call. Anele said troops of Sub-Sector 5 immediately mobilised and pursued the abductors through surrounding bushes, advancing towards Rehina Riverside, where some of the children were found abandoned by the fleeing criminals. She said the troops sustained the pursuit along the river line, rescuing additional victims and bringing the number of recovered children to 18. According to the Army, sustained military pressure forced the abductors to abandon the children as they fled deeper into the surrounding forest. The statement added that troops had extended their search operations along the Ankwa–Kabode–Pachi link road and towards the Awon and Akwondo general areas to locate the remaining four children and apprehend those responsible for the abduction. The Army assured the families of the victims and the general public of its commitment to rescuing all the abducted children. It also said troops would sustain offensive operations and intelligence-led patrols to protect vulnerable communities and prevent further attacks. The military urged residents to remain vigilant and provide timely and credible information to security agencies to support the ongoing search-and-rescue operations and facilitate the arrest of the perpetrators. The post Troops rescue 18 abducted children, hunt for four others in Kaduna appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Laser Focus at the Top of the World
item.description: Earth Observatory Science Earth Observatory Laser Focus at the Top of the… Earth Earth Observatory Image of the Day EO Explorer Topics All Topics Atmosphere Land Heat & Radiation Life on Earth Human Dimensions Natural Events Oceans Remote Sensing Technology Snow & Ice Water More Content Collections Global Maps World of Change Articles Earth Matters Blog Blue Marble: Next Generation EO Kids Mission: Biomes About About Us Subscribe 🛜 RSS Contact Us Search The Ny-Ålesund Geodetic Observatory is located on the west coast of Spitsbergen, an island in Norway’s Svalbard archipelago, shown in this image acquired with the OLI (Operational Land Imager) on Landsat 9 on July 30, 2026. NASA Earth Observatory/Lauren Dauphin More than 60 years ago, scientists at NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center aimed a laser skyward and fired a pulse of light at an orbiting satellite equipped with special reflectors. By measuring the time it took for the light to return, they demonstrated a new, more precise method for tracking satellites. Since then, satellite laser ranging (SLR) has grown more precise and more widely used. The technique now underpins many aspects of Earth observation, such as validating satellite orbits and mapping subtle changes to Earth’s surface. Pioneered at the Goddard Optical Research Facility—now the Goddard Geophysical and Astronomical Observatory —laser ranging is performed at more than 40 stations worldwide. In 2026, the next generation of SLR, developed by NASA scientists and tested at Goddard, began to come online. On October 12, a faster, even more precise SLR system officially debuted at the Ny-Ålesund Geodetic Observatory in Svalbard, Norway, operated by the Norwegian Mapping Authority, a NASA partner. The observatory’s remote location in the Arctic archipelago is shown in this image, acquired with the OLI (Operational Land Imager) on Landsat 9 in July 2026. It is the first NASA next-generation SLR system in operation and the northernmost SLR facility on Earth. While the systems developed decades ago have been “workhorses” of the global laser tracking network, their age and the growing number of satellites have necessitated updates, said Stephen Merkowitz, project manager for NASA’s Space Geodesy Project . “We wanted newer systems that could track more objects, and track them more accurately and precisely,” he said. The Space Geodesy Satellite Laser Ranging system fires at the Ny-Ålesund Geodetic Observatory in Svalbard, Norway, against a backdrop of aurora borealis on October 7, 2026. NASA/Julie Horvath (KBR) Years of development, testing, and careful calibration produced the Space Geodesy Satellite Laser Ranging system now running at Ny-Ålesund. Among its features are lasers that can fire pulses thousands of times per second, up from tens of times per second, and sensors that can detect single photons, meaning that less light needs to be reflected back from a satellite. item.title: GAS: Domestic market gets 41.3% as Nigeria’s supply averages 4.95bcf/d in 10 months
item.description: •LPG retail price rises 12.5% to N1,800 per kg •Make domestic market attractive to secure adequate supply — NALPGAM By Udeme Akpan Despite Nigeria’s 215.19 trillion cubic feet (Tcf) of proven natural gas reserves, the domestic market received an average of 2.04 billion cubic feet per day (bcf/d), representing 41.3 per cent of the country’s total supply of 4.95 bcf/d in the first 10 months of 2026. The Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority, NMDPRA, disclosed this in its latest report obtained by Vanguard. The report showed that the Nigeria LNG Limited, NLNG, received the remaining 58.7 per cent, averaging 2.91 bcf/d. In October, total average daily gas supply rose by 2.7 per cent to 4.951 bcf/d, from 4.822 bcf/d in September. Domestic supply increased by 2.3 per cent to 2.113 bcf/d, while deliveries to NLNG grew by three per cent to 2.838 bcf/d. April recorded the highest average daily supply during the 10-month period at 5.141 bcf/d, comprising 2.01 bcf/d for domestic market and 3.13 bcf/d for NLNG. Gas supply to power plants increased by 10 per cent to 0.571 bcf/d in October. Deliveries to gas-based industries also rose, while supplies to commercial users declined. Supply to the Escravos Gas-to-Liquids facility fell by two per cent. Gas exports also strengthened. Average daily LNG exports increased by seven per cent to 52,721 metric tonnes per day, from 49,198 metric tonnes per day in September, while pipeline exports through the West African Gas Pipeline (WAGP) rose by 11 per cent to 0.149 bcf/d, from 0.134 bcf/d. LPG retail price rises 12.5% to ₦1,800 per kg Meanwhile, the average retail price of liquefied petroleum gas, LPG, also known as cooking gas, rose by 12.5 per cent to ₦1,800 per kilogramme in November 2026, from ₦1,600 in October. Checks by Vanguard attributed the increase largely to limited supply. The average depot price of LPG stood at ₦1,274 in the Daily Depot Price Intelligence Report for Friday, November 20, 2026. The report covered Lagos, Warri, Calabar and Port Harcourt but did not provide a regional breakdown of LPG prices. Make domestic market attractive to secure adequate supply — NALPGAM The Executive Secretary/Chief Executive Officer of the Nigerian Association of Liquefied Petroleum Gas Marketers, NALPGAM, Bassey Essien, told Vanguard in an interview that Nigeria must make its domestic gas market commercially attractive to secure adequate supplies. He said: “Gas exports generate foreign exchange, but the domestic market must also be commercially attractive enough to secure adequate supply. ‘’The solution is not to stop exports but to make the domestic market competitive enough to attract supply while preserving export earnings.” On Domestic Gas Delivery Obligation, DGDO, Essien noted that regulation alone could not guarantee physical deliveries without adequate infrastructure and effective payment systems. “The Domestic Gas Delivery Obligation, DGDO, requires producers to supply the local marke

item.title: President Tinubu does not need this falsehood
item.description: By Dele Sobowale Each time President Tinubu mentions $1 trillion economy by 2030, he reveals more than the politicians’ penchant for making promises they cannot keep. He brings into question his proclaimed economic qualification as an accounting graduate for a Chicago university. There is abundant evidence, provided by Tinubu himself, to call that assertion a deliberate lie. I have touched on some of them before; but, Tinubu, despite expert advice continues to campaign on a promise which can never be redeemed. Here again, the facts which Tinubu stubbornly ignores; because they don’t fit into the narratives of a desperate politician running for elections, will once more be presented. This time fresh evidence will be added from Tinubu’s campaign organization. POLITICS AND FALSEHOOD ARE INSEPRABLE “The great masses of the people ..will fall victims to a great lie than to a small one.” Adolf Hitler, 1899-1945, VANGUARD BOOK OF QUOTATIONS, VBQ p 130. Politicians, under the best of circumstances, would repeat the same falsehood in the hope that saying it long enough will make it true. And, when they fail, they never apologise to the people; they blame others. President Tinubu’s assertion that Nigeria’s economy can grow to $1 trillion by 2030 is the sort of thing Hitler was talking about. I have given Tinubu the benefit of doubt that he read accounting in an American university as an undergraduate. But, his insistence that the Nigerian economy, whose Gross Domestic Product, GDP, is estimated to reach $386.67 billion at the end of the year 2026 could reach $1 trillion in just four years, would have had first year students of any university wondering if that was a joke or something else not hilarious. The figures don’t add up. LIARS CAN FIGURE; FIGURES DON’T LIE “Every government is run by liars and nothing they say should be believed. I.F Stone, 1907-1989. US Journalist and Publisher. Stone was one of my favourite columnists during my ten years in the US. I read his articles as if preparing for an examination on the subject discussed. He always led with evidence. So, let us start with the Federal Governments own figures. President Tinubu has been going round the country telling Nigerians the Nigerian economy is set to grow by 4.5 per cent this year. That will be the best performance since 2014. It is admittedly very commendable but worse than Jonathan’s worst year. The FG is also promising 6 percent growth in 2027. Highly praise-worthy if achieved. For some reason, not too difficult to understand, Tinubu, a self-proclaimed accountant, as well as his mob of supporters, cannot seem to understand that you cannot grow $386.67 billion to $1 trillion at 6 per cent in four years. This is primary school arithmetic called compound interest calculations. It is repeated at freshman level in American universities. Has Tinubu forgotten it or is he just peddling the big lie for political gain? QUANTUM LEAPS OF OTHER VARIABLES NEEDED “Economics is not magic; at its bes

item.title: How Oyibo, BEDC worker was murdered 4 months into marriage
item.description: •Disco, Delta community mourn •Family shattered, seeks justice By Egufe Yafugborhi & Cynthia Alo Oscar Eze, popularly known as Oyibo or NEPA Man, left home on Monday, November 16, 2026, for another routine assignment as an operations personnel of the Benin Electricity Distribution Company, BEDC, Agbor Business Unit. The 38-year-old had no reason to suspect that the day’s work in Umunede, Ika North-East Local Government Area of Delta State, would be his last. Four months after remarrying following the death of his first wife, Eze was brutally murdered in circumstances that have left his pregnant wife, young son and elderly mother devastated, while colleagues and residents mourn a man widely remembered for his cheerful disposition. His last assignment took him to a relatively isolated suburb of Idumu-Oba, with sparsely distributed buildings. While working alongside other workmen at a property apparently undergoing finishing, he was ambushed by a gang of youths. A CCTV camera at the premises captured the horrifying encounter. The assailants accosted him around the small entrance gate, dragged him into the compound and repeatedly stabbed him with daggers as other workmen watched in fear. He sustained multiple injuries to his upper body and died shortly afterwards. He was rushed to hospital, where he was confirmed dead. The police subsequently confirmed that Eze was attacked on November 16, at about 1.15 p.m., during a power disconnection exercise at Ileje Quarters, Umunede. According to BEDC management, the property he had disconnected owed the company almost N300,000 in electricity bills. His attackers allegedly trailed him after the disconnection. A legitimate assignment to earn a living ended in a gruesome killing, leaving a community asking how a familiar electricity worker could have become the target of such violence. A young marriage shattered Beyond the circumstances of his death lies the tragedy of a family whose hopes have been abruptly shattered. Eze’s first wife died about two years ago, leaving him with a son. He subsequently remarried barely four months before his death. His new wife was reportedly pregnant. A neighbour close to the BEDC office affirmed: “His first wife, who had a child for him, died about two years ago. Then he remarried four months ago. “I don’t know where the new wife is from. His former wife was from here (Umunede). Oyibo lived at Idumu-Oba.” At the compound where Eze lived, a neighbour said his wife was taken away on the day news of the killing reached them. “We don’t know anything about it. We were here when they sent the information to us, and even on the same day, they took her (Oyibo’s pregnant wife) away. “Personally, I was surprised when I heard the news. I never had any complaints from anybody that he had a problem with them. To be sincere, he was outgoing.” Describing his relationship with the deceased, the neighbour added: “For us here, we never had any misunderstanding with him ever since. He was very hum

item.title: Bayelsa boat mishap: Tinubu donates N250m to victims’ families, as Shettima visits survivors
item.description: ‎ ‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ‎ ‎ABUJA — PRESIDENT Bola Tinubu has called for stricter enforcement of safety standards on Nigeria’s inland waterways following the tragic boat mishap in Bayelsa State, announcing a N250 million Federal Government donation to support the bereaved families. ‎ ‎He also demanded a thorough investigation into the circumstances surrounding the accident, vowing that the Federal Government would work with relevant authorities and state governments to strengthen vessel inspections, safety compliance and enforcement to prevent further loss of lives. ‎ ‎Vice President Kashim Shettima conveyed the President’s position on Sunday during a condolence visit to Yenagoa, the Bayelsa State capital, following Friday’s boat accident at the Oweikorogha/Otuan River Junction in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area. ‎ ‎Speaking at Government House, Yenagoa, the Vice President said the tragedy had exposed the urgent need to improve safety on inland waterways, particularly in riverine communities where water transportation remains essential to everyday life. ‎ ‎”We cannot accept a situation in which citizens must gamble with their lives simply to move between communities. Geography may determine how people travel, but it must never determine how much protection their lives deserve. A Nigerian travelling by boat is entitled to the same concern for safety as one travelling by road or air,” he said. ‎ ‎Senator Shettima said preliminary reports suggesting that the boat developed a mechanical fault must be thoroughly investigated to establish the circumstances of the accident and identify possible failures in safety procedures. ‎ ‎”We have received preliminary reports concerning the circumstances of this accident, including indications of a possible mechanical failure. These reports must be thoroughly investigated by the appropriate authorities. We must establish what happened, identify any failures in safety procedures and take the necessary steps to prevent a recurrence. ‎ ‎”President Tinubu’s administration will continue working with the relevant authorities and state governments to strengthen safety standards, vessel inspections and enforcement on our inland waterways. The lives of our people are too precious for safety to remain an afterthought,” the Vice President stated. ‎ ‎Expressing grief over the tragedy, VP Shettima described the loss as particularly painful because the victims were travelling to attend a burial ceremony when the accident occurred. ‎ ‎”There is a particular cruelty in the tragedy that has brought us here today. item.title: ECOWAS Monetary Union: Cardoso advocates equity, fairness in governance structure
item.description: By Babajide Komolafe The Governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), Mr. Olayemi Cardoso, has called for equity, fairness and proportional representation in the governance structure of the proposed ECOWAS Monetary Union. He stressed that while regional solidarity and respect for the sovereign equality of member states must remain fundamental principles of the Union, these should be appropriately balanced with the relative financial commitments, responsibilities and risks borne by individual member states, particularly in determining participation in decision-making and governance. Cardoso made the call on Friday, November 20, 2026, in Abidjan, Côte d’Ivoire, on behalf of Nigeria at the Ministerial Session of the 6th Presidential Task Force Meeting on the ECOWAS Single Currency Programme in Abidjan, Cote d’ Ivoire. The Ministerial Committee of the ECOWAS Presidential Task Force comprises Ministers of Finance and Governors of central banks of PTF member states. He described the meeting as a defining milestone in the ECOWAS monetary integration process, noting that deliberations had recently focused on critical considerations regarding the institutional architecture of the proposed Monetary Union, including the location of its institutions, leadership appointments, and the allocation of authority and responsibilities. “The decisions we take today will shape the future of the Union for decades to come,” Cardoso told delegates. “They will influence its credibility in the eyes of investors and development partners, its legitimacy in the eyes of our citizens, and the confidence of Member States that their commitments are being matched by a meaningful voice within the institutions they are helping to build.” He restated Nigeria’s commitment to the ECOWAS Monetary Cooperation Programme and to establishing the ECO, describing it as “longstanding and unwavering” and citing substantial financial contributions, sustained technical support, and compromises made “in the broader interest of regional consensus”. “Nigeria has and will continue to demonstrate solidarity and fairness, respecting the sovereignty of other member states. We remain fully committed to the successful establishment of the ECO and to a Monetary Union that is credible, sustainable and beneficial to all Member States,” Cardoso declared. He, however, maintained that solidarity must be accompanied by equity, arguing that countries with larger economies and greater financial responsibilities should be given fair consideration in the governance of the institutions they support. “While bigger economies continue to take up the burden, they should also be considered to play a significant role because of the risk and systemic importance they have in the sub-region. Above all, such economies need to defend the huge contribution they make before their respective parliaments and the civil society. Where obligations are shared but influence is not, arrangements may be agreed, but their long-term susta

item.title: Watch live today: Amazon launching 1st batch of internet satellites since Vulcan Centaur failure
item.description: null Another batch of Amazon internet satellites will fly on Monday morning (Nov. 23), just eight days after a launch failure doomed 40 of the spacecraft. An Ariane 6 rocket carrying 36 satellites for the Amazon Leo constellation is scheduled to lift off from Europe's Spaceport in Kourou, French Guiana on Monday, during a 29-minute window that opens at 6:09 a.m. EST (1109 GMT; 8:09 a.m. local time in Kourou). You can watch it live here at Space.com, courtesy of Arianespace, the French company that operates the Ariane 6. Coverage will begin about 30 minutes before launch. An Ariane 6 rocket launches 32 Amazon Leo satellites to orbit from French Guiana on Feb. 12, 2026. (Image credit: ESA/CNES/Arianespace-ArianeGroup/Optique Video du CSG-P. Piron) Amazon Leo, so named because it will operate in low Earth orbit , will compete with SpaceX's Starlink internet constellation, which currently consists of more than 11,000 operational spacecraft. Amazon's network will eventually have more than 3,200 satellites, but just 400 or so have reached orbit to date. Another 40 were supposed to be delivered on Nov. 15, but they were lost after their rocket ride, a United Launch Alliance (ULA) Vulcan Centaur , suffered a problem shortly after launch. Ariane 6 and Vulcan Centaur aren't the only rockets Amazon is depending on to build its broadband constellation. Jeff Bezos' company has also booked rides on ULA's Atlas V rocket, Blue Origin's New Glenn and SpaceX's Falcon 9 . Vulcan will be grounded for a while as ULA investigates the Nov. 15 failure and works to fix whatever caused it. And New Glenn hasn't flown since April, when the rocket failed to deliver AST SpaceMobile's BlueBird 7 satellite to the proper orbit. New Glenn's return to flight was further complicated on May 28, when the rocket exploded during a routine prelaunch test. The Ariane 6, the successor to Arianespace's Ariane 5 heavy lifter, debuted in July 2024 and has nine launches under its belt to date. All of them have been successful except that maiden mission, which was a partial failure. Monday's mission will be the fourth Amazon Leo flight for the Ariane 6, following launches in February, April and June of this year.

item.title: Death Toll From Bayelsa Boat Accident Rises To 29
item.description: The death toll from Friday’s boat accident in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State has risen to 29, with over 50 survivors receiving treatment in hospitals. Governor Douye Diri disclosed this during a condolence visit by Vice President Kashim Shettima. Diri explained that the final casualty figure had yet to be established as efforts were still ongoing to recover the affected vessel. ﻿ He, however, said some passengers might still be trapped inside the boat. The governor described the incident as avoidable, alleging that the boat was not fit for river travel and had operated from an unauthorised loading point. He said the state government had taken responsibility for the medical bills and feeding of the survivors. Diri thanked President Tinubu for the concern shown by the Presidency since the incident occurred, particularly the Vice President’s visit to the state. He used the occasion to appeal for Federal Government support for the construction of more roads across Bayelsa, noting that improved road access would reduce the dependence of some communities on water transportation. The accident occurred on Friday, November 20, 2026, when a boat conveying mourners to a burial ceremony capsized near Oweikorogha Community in the Ukubie area of Southern Ijaw. The Bayelsa State Police Command confirmed the incident in a statement, adding that the boat was travelling from Ayama Community to Ukubie for a burial ceremony on Friday, when it capsized at about 11 a.m. The boat developed a mechanical fault while navigating the waterways, according to a preliminary police report. Following the incident, rescue operations were launched, with several passengers rescued while others were initially reported missing. A survivor had also alleged that the wooden passenger boat, popularly known as a ‘love boat’, was overloaded with passengers and their belongings. President Bola Tinubu expressed condolences to the families of the victims, describing the incident as tragic and directing relevant federal disaster response agencies to support rescue and recovery efforts. He also approved ₦250 million in support for the families of the victims. The post Death Toll From Bayelsa Boat Accident Rises To 29 appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Global Climate Talks Collapse In Chaotic End To COP31
item.description: The COP31 climate talks failed Sunday as a contentious deal collapsed over fossil fuels and the summit in Turkey stretched into record overtime. The final agreement was rejected in a chaotic finale to a UN climate summit that ran two days over schedule, underscoring the strains on diplomacy in an increasingly fractured world. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, who urged nations to send fossil fuels “the way of the dinosaurs” during a fiery appearance at the talks, expressed deep dismay. “I share the very profound frustration of all those who expected governments to rise to the moment the climate crisis demands,” the outgoing UN chief said in a statement. COP31 negotiations chair Chris Bowen, who unsuccessfully sought to broker consensus among nearly 200 nations, conceded he could not overcome what he called “unbridgeable red lines”. “Unfortunately, we were unable to reach agreement on a cover decision… And that’s disappointing. Very disappointing,” Bowen, who is Australia’s climate minister, told a throng of reporters. More than 49 hours after the summit was supposed to end, COP31 President and Turkish Environment Minister Murat Kurum banged the gavel to conclude the marathon talks. COP31 President and Turkey’s Minister of Environment, Urbanisation and Climate Change Murat Kurum speaks with the media following a plenary session during the United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) at the Antalya Expo Centre, in Antalya on November 22, 2026. Calls For Reform Bowen said the summit backdrop was “the most complicated and fraught geopolitical environment in living memory”, as soaring energy prices and fallout from the Middle East war complicated the search for unity. Under pressure to show progress in a year of climate-linked disasters from Europe to Nepal, Bowen sought an overarching “cover decision” to prove countries were still united in tackling the crisis. But his plan unravelled as familiar fault lines emerged over fossil fuels, with the EU and Saudi Arabia locking horns over the pace of the shift away from coal, oil and gas. The negotiations stalled as oil-producing states blocked any mention of phasing out fossil fuels in the final deal. “We will not endorse a cover decision… that does not even mention fossil fuels, which is the key driver of climate change,” said Ireland’s climate minister, Darragh O’Brien, whose country holds the rotating EU presidency. “And we will not accept a COP that greenwashes fossil fuels.” Panama, Vanuatu and the Marshall Islands also objected, and as the deal imploded, COP31 became the longest climate summit on record. Former US vice president and climate advocate Al Gore said it was “outrageous that a handful of petrostates have veto power over any mention of fossil fuels”. The COP process is “in need of significant reform”, Gore said on X, as most countries sought “to move forward in good faith.” COP31 President and Turkey’s Minister of Environment, Urbanisation and Climate Change Murat Kurum (C) attends

item.description: 7 Min Read 65 Years of Human Spaceflight at NASA Johnson NASA astronaut Randy Bresnik, ESA (European Space Agency) astronaut Luca Parmitano, former NASA astronaut Russell “Rusty” Schweickart, and NASA astronauts Frank Rubio and Bob Hines appear onstage at the Artemis Celebration Gala at the Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex in Merritt Island, Florida, on Nov. 6, 2026. Credits: Purpose Entertainment/Shanna Lockwood Employees and guests of NASA’s Johnson Space Center celebrate the center’s 65th anniversary at the Lunar Receiving Park in Houston on Nov. 19, 2026. NASA/Robert Markowitz For 65 years, NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston has helped shape human spaceflight, from the Gemini missions that demonstrated rendezvous and docking techniques needed for Apollo to the research conducted aboard the International Space Station, which has supported a continuous human presence for more than 26 years. Today, Johnson teams are preparing crews and systems for NASA’s next chapter: returning astronauts to the lunar surface and building the capabilities needed for a long-term human presence at the Moon. Across those missions, generations of flight controllers, engineers, scientists, instructors, medical specialists, and other experts have helped crews live and work beyond Earth. Johnson is home to NASA’s Orion and Moon Base programs, and its teams continue to support space station operations, astronaut training, spacecraft development, mission operations, and human health. Mercury and Gemini: Preparing for Apollo When the Manned Spacecraft Center officially opened on Nov. 1, 1961, NASA had already flown two suborbital Mercury missions, with the first orbital flight just months away. Most Project Mercury activities remained at Cape Canaveral in Florida to maintain continuity, but the new Project Gemini took up residence in Houston, housed in temporary leased facilities across the city while construction of the new Clear Lake campus continued. The new Mission Control Center became NASA’s primary flight control center in June 1965, with the Gemini IV mission that included the first American spacewalk. Houston became the nerve center for American human spaceflight, overseeing the remaining eight Gemini missions before transitioning to the Apollo program. Following the tragic Apollo 1 fire in January 1967, managers, engineers, and astronauts at the Manned Spacecraft Center applied lessons learned to make the spacecraft safer and ensure the safety of its astronauts, resuming crewed missions in October 1968. Managers in Houston devised a daring plan to send Apollo 8 on a circumlunar flight. In December 1968, Apollo 8 made its historic trip around the Moon, and seven months later Apollo 11 astronauts Neil Armstrong and Edwin “Buzz” Aldrin landed on the lunar surface. Their first voice transmission back to Earth after their arrival began with the word “Houston.” Five more Moon landings completed the Apollo program and humanity’s first phase of lunar exploration

item.title: SpaceX launches 2 rockets from same pad 32 hours apart, smashing turnaround record (video)
item.description: null SpaceX set a new record with its latest satellite launch out of California. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base 's Launch Complex-4E on Sunday (Nov. 22) at 7:23 a.m. ET (1223 GMT; 4:23 a.m. local time in California), on a mission for the U.S. National Reconnaissance Office (NRO) called NROL-136. It was the second launch from that pad in a little over 32 hours, after the USSF-317 mission for the U.S. Space Force . And that quick turnaround made history. Massive high five to the @SpaceX west coast team for a world record launch to launch turn from Pad 4e last night! 32 hr, 3 min, 21 sec! This smashed the previous record of 45 hrs from Pad 40. Team got there with several hours of margin. Next goal… the 24 hr turn! 🏎️🚀🏎️🚀 November 22, 2026 "Massive high five to the @SpaceX west coast team for a world record launch to launch turn from Pad 4e last night! 32 hr, 3 min, 21 sec! This smashed the previous record of 45 hrs from Pad 40. Team got there with several hours of margin. Next goal… the 24 hr turn!" Kiko Dontchev, SpaceX's vice president of launch, said via X on Sunday . (Pad 40 is at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida.) NROL-136 was the sixth launch of 2026 so far for the NRO. All of them have been carried out by SpaceX 's workhorse Falcon 9, and all have delivered classified satellites to low Earth orbit . The launch marked another step in the NRO's effort to expand its intelligence-gathering capabilities through a proliferated network of spacecraft designed to provide more frequent and timely surveillance of locations around the globe. About two minutes after liftoff, the Falcon 9's first-stage booster separated from the rocket's upper stage, which continued carrying the classified payloads onward to orbit. The booster then reversed course and returned to Vandenberg, touching down at Landing Zone 4 approximately seven and a half minutes after launch. Saturday's launch was the 14th flight for this particular Falcon 9 booster, dubbed B1097, which previously launched NASA 's Sentinel-6B ocean-monitoring satellite, NROL-172, USSF-259 for the Space Force, and eight Starlink missions. NROL-136 was the 15th launch dedicated to building the NRO's "proliferated architecture," the satellites for which have been developed in partnership with SpaceX and Northrop Grumman. The network is designed to increase coverage and improve the "capability and resilience" of U.S. intelligence operations in space , according to the NRO's mission website . The NRO began deploying the constellation in May 2024 with the launch of NROL-146. The most recent proliferated architecture mission before Sunday was NROL-179, which lifted off on June 19, 2026. As with any classified mission, the agency has not disclosed the exact number of satellites aboard NROL-136 or revealed details about their onboard technologies. item.title: This viral star projector has been hyped to Mars and back, but we hunted down the best version you can buy
item.description: It was only a matter of time, but AI has come for astronomy accessories. I’ve yet to see a fictional elderly craftsman begging you to buy his hand-carved telescopes; however, it has absolutely muddied the waters around this viral gooseneck Galaxy Projector Night Light. The good news is that there is an impressive little star projector to be had here, and I’m here to cut through the AI-assisted hype. To make sure you’re not hoodwinked, I’ve done the online legwork to bring you the best version of this device, and it won’t cost you a fortune to put a planetarium in your pocket. Before we dive into what makes this Galaxy Projector Night Light so great, there are a couple of pressing issues to address. No variant of this USB-powered star projector will break up heated dinner arguments by casting a beautifully animated space whale on the ceiling, as one ridiculous AI-generated advert asserts. Its projections are eye-catching enough to entertain space fans young and old, but they’re strictly static. Also, while you might be tempted by the lure of 24 interchangeable slides, compared to this Galaxy Projector Night Light’s 13, this lesser model’s slide selection is a letdown. Not only are the slides smaller and blurrier than this model, a large number are dedicated to seasonal holidays. As much as I enjoy Christmas, if I had Santa’s colossal face gazing down at me from the ceiling I’d never sleep again. Zanbix 2 in 1 Galaxy Projector Night Light review More than meets the eye Aside from the projector itself, the Zanbix 2 in 1 Galaxy Projector Night Light includes 13 swappable slides, crammed into a compact box. (Image credit: Chris McMullen) I tempered my expectations when I first got my hands on the Galaxy Projector Night Light. Packed in a small, relatively unassuming box, it looks remarkably similar to the standard model that’s spread across TikTok, YouTube, Facebook and so on. Just like that one, it’s powered via USB, with a flexible stalk, a slot for slides and a nose-mounted focus wheel. However, once I hooked it up to a handy USB socket, all my reservations vanished, and I was seriously impressed by the power of this little projector. You’ll need a darkened room but the Galaxy Projector Night Light’s larger lens is a serious step-up from the run-of-the-mill version. Its images are richer and clearer than you’d expect from a projector this size, and easily capable of transforming a mid-sized ceiling or wall into a cosmic display. This stunning image of the Pillars of Creation originally came from the James Webb Space Telescope. (Image credit: Chris McMullen) This stunning James Webb Space Telescope image of the Pillars of Creation, with its vast columns of gas and dust, is a perfect example of the projections on offer. The fact the display was static didn’t diminish its wow factor, and I spent a good 15 minutes gazing at it in wonder. The Galaxy Projector Night Light does have a four-hour shut-off in case you drift off or want to use it

item.title: As 'Star Trek: First Contact' turns 30, Director Jonathan Frakes reflects on his triumphant time-travel blockbuster (interview)
item.description: null " Star Trek: First Contact " celebrates its 30th anniversary today, and the engaging sci-fi classic still looks fantastic three decades later. With the sad passing of its star, Patrick Stewart , last month, and "Star Trek's" milestone 60th birthday taking place in 2026, this is a bittersweet salute that also holds an extra special significance. Directed by "The Next Generation's" Number One, Jonathan Frakes , in his feature film debut, " First Contact " consistently ranks as one of the finest "Star Trek" feature films among fans and critics, and those accolades are well deserved. Based on a compelling screenplay by Brannon Braga and Ronald D. Moore, "First Contact" remains as bright and beautiful as ever, brimming with bravado, heart, horror, and heroism. Not only was it a bona fide crowdpleaser when it was released by Paramount over Thanksgiving week on Nov. 22, 1996, but it was also a financial success for the studio, eventually pulling in a worldwide total of $212 million off a modest $45 million budget. Honestly, who can forget Alice Krige's seductive Borg Queen, Marina Sirtis’ Deana Troi tipsy on tequila, Brent Spiner's Data feeling the sensation of human skin, Patrick Stewart’s Jean-Luc Picard reliving past traumas, and James Cromwell's Zephram Cochrane blasting off in the Phoenix and dancing to Roy Orbison's "Ooby Dooby"? We caught up with Frakes for "First Contact's" 30th anniversary to hear why this "Trek" treasure holds up and warp back to Hollywood’s heyday of the '90s. Resistance is futile! "What’s not to love?" Frakes tells SPACE regarding the film’s lasting popularity. "It was bulletproof. Dean Devlin ["Stargate," "Independence Day"] and I have very similar sensibilities about filmmaking. We like the whole idea of action, adventure, comedy, and in the case of 'First Contact,' a little horror as well. ILM’s John Knoll, the guy who won the Oscar for 'Star Wars,' just happened to be our Special Effects Supervisor." "Star Trek: First Contact" celebrates its 30th birthday on Nov. 22, 2026. (Image credit: Paramount) "First Contact" is filled with memorable moments and indelible performances, some of which certainly stand out for Frakes looking back over the years on the production. "The two things that always come to mind were the beautiful scene with Alfre [Woodard] and Patrick, the Moby Dick scene, where she says, 'You broke your little ships,'" he recalls. "I was sitting under the camera with my face in my hands, watching two heavyweights go at it take after take. It was what you dream of. They were into it. The writing was great. We had time to do it right, and they were fabulous together. "That and the Cromwell and Marina drunk on tequila scene. It's not only one extended take, but it contributes to the pace of the movie in the right kind of way. My wife tells me that I was really good in that scene because I was exhausted and relaxed. item.title: On this day in space! Nov.22, 1989: NASA launches space shuttle Discovery on classified STS-33 mission for the US military
item.description: null On Nov. 22, 1989, the space shuttle Discovery launched on the secret mission STS-33 for the U.S. military. It lifted off from Kennedy Space Center and up into the dark of night. This was the third nighttime launch of the shuttle program and the 32nd shuttle mission overall. Discovery had five astronauts on board. Their mission was to deploy a classified payload for the U.S. Department of Defense. NASA and the military launched several secretive shuttle missions to deploy military satellites . The satellite that launched with STS-33 is believed to be a type of spy satellite called Magnum. But exactly what Magnum was doing in orbit remains classified. NASA's space shuttle Discovery launches on the classified STS-33 mission for the U.S. military on Nov. 22, 1989. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered From its start, the Space Transportation System, better known as the space shuttle, was a compromise between meeting civilian and military needs. NASA saw the vehicle as a means of supporting science research, establishing an on-orbit economy (servicing commercial satellites and flying company payloads) and ultimately, assembling the parts for a space station. The Department of Defense saw the shuttle as an asset to deploying and retrieving reconnaissance satellites, among other projects, some of them classified. It was not until the loss of the space shuttle Challenger, that it was decided that the shuttle would only be used by the military when it was key to national security. Other needs would be met by expendable launch vehicles (ELVs). As an aside, the STS-33 astronauts also spent Thanksgiving in space during this mission. But the holiday was off to a crappy start when the shuttle's toilet broke first thing in the morning. After spending most of the day fixing it, they got to enjoy their Thanksgiving turkey together. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

item.title: Israel investigates West Bank fires
item.description: Israeli authorities have opened an investigation after Palestinian vehicles and properties were vandalised and set on fire in four villages in the occupied West Bank, in attacks local activists say were carried out by Israeli settlers. Around eight vehicles were reportedly torched and racist slogans sprayed on walls, prompting Israeli soldiers and police to deploy to the area. The attacks come amid a surge in settler violence since the outbreak of the Gaza war in October 2023, with more than 1,100 Palestinians killed by Israeli soldiers or settlers in the West Bank since then, according to an AFP tally. They also follow recent sanctions announced by the UK and Australia against eight Israeli companies involved in settlement activity. France 24 correspondent Noga Tarnopolsky shares further details from Jerusalem.

item.title: Rema & Wizkid Have Us Singing Along to “Feel Alright” With This New Lyric Video
item.description: Scene from the official lyric video for Rema and Wizkid’s “Feel Alright” off the seven-track EP E-Mortal Boy (EMB). If you have been singing along to “ Feel Alright ” since E-Mortal Boy came out, Rema has just dropped the official lyric video so you can finally catch every single line without guessing. Having the words on screen makes it much easier to follow how Rema and Wizkid trade verses on the opening track, mixing smooth R&B-leaning melodies with English, Nigerian Pidgin and Yoruba slang as they serenade a love interest. For plenty of listeners, “Feel Alright” is the biggest talking point on E-Mortal Boy because it marks the very first official collaboration between Rema and Wizkid, bringing two distinct Afrobeats eras together right at the start of the project. Putting out a lyric video for the track gives fans of both artists a chance to properly take in the lyrics and harmonies that have had the song on heavy rotation since the project landed. The release also keeps the spotlight on E-Mortal Boy, Rema’s seven-track EP that followed earlier singles “TEA” and “Oh No”. Alongside “Feel Alright” with Wizkid, the project includes “Velvet”, “TANZANIA” with BNYX, “SUGA” with Theodora , and closer “Bang Bang” with London and Kah-Lo , showing off the wide range of sounds Rema pulls together across the seven songs. If you have been waiting to learn every word of Rema and Wizkid’s first joint record, this lyric video has you covered. item.title: How Tamagotchis got us hooked on digital pets
item.description: If you were are a kid in the late 1990s, there's a near-100 percent chance you either had a Tamagotchi or knew someone who did. The tiny digital pets came out of nowhere and became an overnight sensation, as millions of kids signed up to parent a crying, hungry, constantly dirty creature. Until they went to school, anyway, at which point their parents were given some new responsibilities they neither asked for nor wanted. On this episode of Version History, we dig deep into the story of the Tamagotchi. That story has its 30th anniversary this week, even though the real craze only lasted a few years. David Pierce is joined by The Verge's Mia … Read the full story at The Verge.

item.title: GLP-1 drugs could have a surprisingly large environmental payoff
item.description: GLP-1 weight-loss medicines such as Ozempic and Wegovy could affect much more than the waistlines of the people who take them. If widely used, our new research suggests these appetite-suppressing medicines could transform the global food system and free up vast areas of agricultural land. The global food system is ultimately driven by demand. If people eat less, producers respond, affecting production, prices, trade, and how much land is needed. We used a powerful computer simulation to explore scenarios ranging from GLP-1 use concentrated in high-income countries to widespread global access. With widespread use of these medicines among adults living with obesity, we estimate that reduced calorie intake could prevent up to 6.6 million deaths each year by 2050, while freeing up as much as 32 million hectares of agricultural land—an area slightly larger than Italy—for other uses. item.title: Elizabeth Agboola: Your Next Flight From Nigeria Could Be Two Holidays in One. Here’s How
item.description: Have you ever spent six hours in an airport waiting for your connecting flight, watching the departure screens, browsing duty-free shops and wondering what the city outside looks like? Perhaps you were connecting through Istanbul, Doha, Dubai or Addis Ababa. You were technically in another country, but the closest you came to experiencing it was buying a souvenir at the airport. What if I told you that some airlines could help you turn that connection into an additional holiday, sometimes even providing accommodation? Having travelled to more than 70 countries, I have learnt that one of the smartest ways to travel is to pay attention to the journey, not just the destination. Many Nigerians book international tickets based on price, travel time and baggage allowance. These are important considerations, but there is another question worth asking: What else can this ticket give me? I am talking about stopovers, not the hurried two-hour connection where you are running between terminals, but an intentional break in your journey that allows you to experience another destination before continuing to the country you originally planned to visit. And with the right airline, itinerary and travel documents, that additional experience might cost less than you imagine. First, Understand What You Are Booking A layover is generally a connection between flights; a stopover is a longer, planned break in your journey. Airlines define these differently, and the distinction matters because some offer special hotel packages, sightseeing tours or complimentary accommodation to qualifying passengers. For example, imagine travelling from Lagos to London through Istanbul. Instead of spending a few hours at Istanbul Airport, you could investigate whether your ticket qualifies for a longer stopover, allowing you to explore Istanbul before continuing to London. You have now turned one international journey into an opportunity to experience two destinations outside Nigeria. The secret is to investigate the stopover before purchasing your ticket, rather than arriving at the airport and hoping the airline will allow you to stay longer. Turkish Airlines: Turn Istanbul Into Part of Your Holiday Turkish Airlines operates a Stopover in Istanbul programme for eligible international passengers connecting through Istanbul Airport. For visa purposes, Nigerians do not qualify, but with a valid Turkish visa you would be able to qualify for some of the perks. Qualifying travellers with connections of at least 20 hours and up to seven days may receive complimentary hotel accommodation. Under the standard programme, eligible Economy Class passengers can receive one night in a four-star hotel, while Business Class passengers may receive two nights in a five-star or boutique hotel. Imagine travelling from Abuja or Lagos through Istanbul to London, Paris or another European destination. item.title: 10 things that worry me about chasing the 2027 total solar eclipse in Egypt
item.description: null On Aug. 2, 2027, I'll be in Luxor, Egypt, to witness what could be the greatest total solar eclipse of my life. I've seen nine total solar eclipses across the world, but this one promises to be different. For a remarkable six minutes and 22 seconds, the moon will completely cover the sun, plunging Egypt's ancient temples and monuments into eerie twilight as the solar corona bursts into view. I've been calling it the "eclipse of the century" for many years, and for good reason. It will be the longest total solar eclipse until 2114 — and the longest on land of the 21st century — and it will take place in one of the most extraordinary places on Earth. What could go wrong? I've chased eclipses long enough to know that the celestial mechanics are the easy part. The moon will arrive exactly on schedule — that's guaranteed. Everything else — the weather, the crowds, the transport, the equipment and the people — is rather less predictable. From the possibility of dust storms to uncertainty about whether boats will even be allowed to move on the Nile, there are plenty of reasons to be slightly wary about what awaits eclipse chasers after the ultimate bragging rights on Aug. 2, 2027. Here are the 10 things worrying me most about the 2027 total solar eclipse in Egypt. A dust storm could make the eclipsed sun less impressive. (Image credit: Grant Faint via Getty Images) 1. A sudden dust storm The chances of cloud-free skies in Luxor and anywhere in Upper Egypt in August are exceptionally high — close to 100%. That's almost unheard of in eclipse-chasing. However, clouds aren't the only thing that can obscure the sun. Dust and sand are potential hazards in the Egyptian desert, and a dust storm at the wrong moment could affect—though probably not ruin—the view. Although the sun will almost certainly be visible during the eclipse, airborne dust could hide the delicate structure of the solar corona. 2. Chaos in Luxor How many people will descend on Luxor for the eclipse? August is normally a quiet month for tourism in Luxor because of the oppressive heat. In 2027, however, the city and its surrounding urban area — population about four million — could swell as eclipse chasers, tour groups, photographers and curious visitors descend. Hotels, roads, buses and archaeological sites will all face extraordinary pressure. My biggest concern isn't necessarily the number of people watching the eclipse, but the logistical chaos it will create. Let's take Mallorca as an example for the 2026 eclipse. Authorities there had a plan for its west coast, the prime viewing region. "They were going to start closing roads from 3 p.m. on the afternoon of the eclipse," said Simon Waldram , who runs astrophotography and landscape photography workshops and who drove his tour group to the intended viewing location at 8 o'clock on the morning of the eclipse. "There were already 300 cars there, and by 11 a.m. they had shut the road." Official plans can quickly change. The banks of the

On Saturday night, Lionel Messi's Inter Miami played the first leg of their opening-round playoff tie against Columbus Crew, a match that turned into a nightmare for the Florida side. Whatever the case, the Florida club face an uphill battle to reach the next round of the playoffs, with a three-goal deficit to overturn away at Columbus Crew next Saturday. item.title: APOD: 2026 November 22 – Swirls and Colors on Jupiter from Juno
item.description: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 22 –… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Swirls and Colors on Jupiter from Juno Explanation: What creates the colors in Jupiter’s clouds? No one is sure. The thick atmosphere of Jupiter is mostly hydrogen and helium , elements which are colorless at the low temperatures of the Jovian cloud tops . Which trace molecules provide the colors remains a topic of research , although small amounts of ammonium hydrosulfide are one leading candidate . What is clear from the featured color-enhanced image — and many similar images — is that lighter clouds are typically higher up than darker ones. Pictured, light clouds swirl around reddish regions toward the lower right, while they appear to cover over some darker domains on the upper right. The featured image was taken by the robotic Juno spacecraft in 2018 during its 14th low pass over Jupiter . Juno continues in its looping elliptical orbit, swooping near the huge planet every 33 days and exploring a slightly different sector each time around. item.title: Review: Godzilla Minus Zero joins the list of truly stellar sequels
item.description: It's a rare thing for a film sequel to match or even surpass its predecessor; The Godfather Part II and Terminator 2: Judgement Day are the best known examples on a pretty short list. Go ahead and add Godzilla Minus Zero to that list. Director Takashi Yamazaki's sequel to his critically acclaimed Godzilla Minus One (2023) is everything one could want in a Godzilla movie: human pathos, great special effects, and, ultimately, two giant kaiju duking it out over who gets to destroy Japan (and eventually the world) the most. (Spoilers for the first film below. Spoilers for Minus Zero but no major reveals until after the gallery. We'll give you a heads-up when we get there.) As I wrote previously , Yamazaki wanted to return to Godzilla’s filmic roots with Minus One , setting the events in postwar Japan and tapping into the monster’s symbolic representation of the Japanese perspective on the 1940s nuclear holocaust—while also incorporating all-too-human themes of guilt and redemption. That first film focused on kamikaze pilot Kōichi Shikishima (Ryunosuke Kamiki), who struggled with survivor’s guilt after he failed to take action when Godzilla attacked the Japanese base on Odo Island in 1945. item.title: On this day in space! Nov. 21, 1676: Danish astronomer discovers speed of light — by accident — while observing Jupiter's moon Io
item.description: null On Nov. 21, 1676, the Danish astronomer Ole Rømer discovered the speed of light . Before Rømer figured it out, scientists thought that light travels instantaneously, or infinitely fast. Rømer disproved this almost by accident when he was studying Jupiter's moon Io . He was trying to figure out how long it takes Io to orbit Jupiter in hopes of using it as a cosmic clock. He watched Io disappear behind Jupiter and reappear on the other side. He did this over and over every 42 hours for years. To his surprise, the timing of the eclipses was not consistent. When Earth was closest to Jupiter, the eclipses happened 11 minutes early. Likewise, when the two planets were farthest away, the eclipses were 11 minutes behind schedule. Rømer figured out the pattern and made an accurate prediction for Io's eclipse on Nov. 9, 1676. Then on Nov. 21, he took his findings to the Royal Academy of Sciences and explained that a finite speed of light must be responsible. Danish astronomer Ole Rømer (Image credit: Wikimedia Commons) Why it mattered Understanding that the speed of light is a constant is the key that opened our ability to gauge the scale of the universe, as well as was central to developing modern physics. "The speed of light becomes a sort of ultimate speed limit," Live Science explained in an article about why the speed of light matters. "In fact, objects with mass, be they cars or neutrinos, can't reach the speed of light because they would need infinite energy to do so."

item.title: 'Star Trek: First Contact' at 30: Resistance is futile when it comes to the 'Next Generation' crew's greatest big-screen adventure
item.description:
Richard's love affair with outer space started when he saw the original "Star Wars" on TV aged four, and he spent much of the ’90s watching "Star Trek”, "Babylon 5” and “The X-Files" with his mum. After studying physics at university, he became a journalist, swapped science fact for science fiction, and hit the jackpot when he joined the team at SFX, the UK's biggest sci-fi and fantasy magazine. He liked it so much he stayed there for 12 years, four of them as editor. 

He's since gone freelance and passes his time writing about "Star Wars", "Star Trek" and superheroes for the likes of SFX, Total Film, TechRadar and GamesRadar+. He has met five Doctors, two Starfleet captains and one Luke Skywalker, and once sat in the cockpit of "Red Dwarf"'s Starbug.  

Following the sad news of Sir Patrick Stewart's passing , there's been no shortage of discussion about his best moments as Captain Jean-Luc Picard . "The Inner Light"'s life in 25 minutes is a strong contender, as are the courtroom grandstanding in "The Measure of a Man" and his insistence (under extreme torture) that "there are four lights!" in "Chain of Command". But for this writer's money, it's hard to look past a nine-minute sequence in "Star Trek: First Contact", which turns 30 this weekend. With the Borg overrunning the newly launched USS Enterprise-E, Picard — who has long-standing beef with the Collective, following his assimilation in classic "The Next Generation" story " The Best of Both Worlds " — orders his crew to fight the cybernetic nasties hand-to-hand if required, defying their pleas to activate the ship's self-destruct system and retreat. He even calls Worf — not a man renowned for dodging a fight — a coward, prompting the Klingon to respond that, "If you were any other man, I would kill you where you stand." Ouch. But following some impassioned talk about making the Borg "pay for what they've done", he's finally talked down from his rage by 21st-century stowaway Lily Sloane (Alfre Woodard). She points out that his Moby-Dick-esque obsession is on the verge of going full Ahab, and he eventually sees sense, issuing the order to abandon the Enterprise and destroy the hive. It's a masterclass showcasing the ever-brilliant Stewart's impressive range, as the out-of-control captain's rarely seen temper reaches fever pitch, before normal service is resumed. His subsequent apology to Worf — "As a matter of fact, I think you're the bravest man I've ever known" — is simply perfect. And just as the franchise's zenith, "The Wrath of Khan", is built around Kirk and Khan's decades-old feud, "First Contact" is precision engineered to get the most out of Jean-Luc. This was the right "Star Trek" at the right time, a film that put "TNG"'s greatest villains on a collision course with the origins of Starfleet. It's not quite "Khan", of course — what is? — but it deserves to be mentioned in the same breath. (Image credit: Paramount) In 1996, the "odd numbers bad, even num
